2

Syntax

As suggested in the introduction, dTT is based on a modal type theory roughly in the style of
[
GKNB21
,
GCK+22
]
, with two modes, one for discrete types and one for (augmented semi-)simplicial types.
It then adds a notion of
‘display’
at the simplicial mode that partially internalises unary parametricity.

In addition, the general form of display, which is needed to state the computation rules for simple display, incorporates dependence on an arbitrary telescope (i.e. context extension).
Thus, we also have to include a calculus of telescopes in the theory.
5
5

5

It would probably be possible to collapse this to dependence on a single type, using
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types instead of telescope extension, as in
[
ACKS24
]
, but this would be unaesthetic and less practical for implementation.

The fully general calculus of telescopes and display involves a lot of operations, but in syntax and in most models they are all definable from a smaller number of primitives.

This section is organised as follows.
In
section

2.1
we define the mode theory, which is a 2-category describing the structure of the modal operators.
Then in
section

2.2
we give the rules for the underlying modal type theory, with modalities but not display.

In
section

2.3
we introduce the most basic notions of the telescope calculus: telescopes, partial substitutions (elements of telescopes), and types and terms dependent on a specified telescope (which we call
‘meta-abstractions’
).
These basic notions suffice to give the rules for display, defined mutually with a similar but non-indexed operation on telescopes that we call décalage, in
section

2.4
.

The remaining two sections introduce further operations that are all essentially
‘definable’
in terms of the previous ones.
This is not strictly true at the level of algebraic syntax, where telescopes are just an additional sort of a generalised algebraic theory.
But in a model where telescopes are defined to be finite lists of types — which is an option in any model, both the free syntactic model and in semantic models arising from categories — the laws satisfied by these operations characterise them uniquely.
Specifically, in
section

2.5
we introduce meta-abstracted telescopes, telescope concatenation, and
\Pi
-telescopes, and then in
section

2.6
we introduce display for telescopes, and décalage for dependent telescopes.
These operations will be used in
section

3
to formulate displayed coinductive types, including the type of semi-simplicial types.

2.1

T
he mode theory

We begin with a modal type theory based on the following 2-category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
:

•

there are two modes (objects),
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}
for
discrete
and
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
for

simplicial

•

there are five nonidentity morphisms, forming hom-posets:

\displaystyle\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}},\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}})

\displaystyle=\left\{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}\right\}

\displaystyle\qquad\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}},\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}})

\displaystyle=\left\{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\right\}

\displaystyle\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}},\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}})

\displaystyle=\left\{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\leq{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}\right\}

\displaystyle\qquad\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}},\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}})

\displaystyle=\left\{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\leq{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}\right\}

•

composition is defined by the following tables (plus identity laws)

\begin{array}[]{cc|cccc}&&\lx@intercol\hfil{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\rho}\hfil\lx@intercol\\
&{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\rho}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\\
\hline\cr\hbox{\multirowsetup${\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}$}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}&{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\\
&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}&{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\\
&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\\
&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\end{array}\qquad\begin{array}[]{cc|cc}&&\lx@intercol\hfil{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\rho}\hfil\lx@intercol\\
&{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\rho}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\\
\hline\cr{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}&{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\end{array}

Intuitively,
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
takes a discrete type and forms the constant (augmented semi-)simplicial type, while
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
takes the
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}})
-simplices of an (augmented semi-)simplicial type and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
takes the limit of an (augmented semi-)simplicial diagram.

One verifies that the following adjunctions hold in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
:

{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}\dashv{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\dashv{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}\dashv{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\dashv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}

Thus every morphism in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
, except for
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}
, has a right
adjoint. We refer to the morphisms
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}
as
hazardous
, and
the others
safe
.

\triangleleft

2.2

T
he modal type theory

The basic syntactic structure of dTT follows MTT
[
GKNB21
]
.
Following Coquand, we parametrize the type judgment by a universe level; we assume these form a linear hierarchy generated by
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lzero}}
and
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lsuc}}
, with a join operation
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}
, giving the judgement
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\;\mathsf{level}
.
Each mode has
its contexts, substitutions, types, and terms, so we have the following
judgements where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
denotes an arbitrary mode (
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}
or
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
).

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}

Formally speaking, the inference rules we will give below for these judgments should be interpreted as defining a Generalised Algebraic Theory with these four generating sorts.
Later, we will also introduce some additional sorts.

2.2.1
Contexts

Contexts are built up from the empty contexts by extending with modally
annotated variables and applying locks associated to modalities:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\;\mathsf{mode}}{{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}}{\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\right)\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}}

We additionally enforce the functoriality of locking, and the fact that some
locks preserve empty contexts.

\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\right)\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}\right)\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}}\right)\left({\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\right)\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\left({\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\right)\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}

In fact, the last equality follows from the other three, since
\left({\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\right)=\left({\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\right)=\left({\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\circ{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}\right)=\left({\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}}\right)={\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}
.
Note that
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
does
not
preserve empty contexts.

These equalities mean that contexts no longer have a unique presentation using
the above rules. However, there are ways to select a canonical presentation for
any context. One is to interpret the above equalities as directed rewrites and
work with context presentations that are normal for this rewriting system; thus
there are no identity locks, no repeated locks, and
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
and
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
never occur immediately after an empty context.
Another way is to require that exactly one lock appears in between
any two variables.

Semantically, each lock is left adjoint to its corresponding modality.
Thus,
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
is semantically the same as
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
, while
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
is semantically the same as
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
.
The other lock,
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
, is not reified internally by a modality: intuitively, it takes a discrete type and makes it an (augmented semi-)simplicial type that is
empty
at all dimensions
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}>{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}
.

In particular,
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
and
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
have the further left adjoints
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
and
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
, respectively, so that we will be able to represent their modalities
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
in Fitch-style as in
[
GCK+22
,
Shu23
]
.

As far as
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
goes, we can say that it is fully faithful and hence an equivalence onto its image, which consists of the simplicial types that are empty in dimensions
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}>{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}
.
Moreover, since the initial object is strict, this subcategory is a
sieve
: if we have a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
lies in this subcategory, then so does
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
.
Therefore, while
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
is not a right adjoint, it is a
parametric
right adjoint, so we can still use the method of of
[
GCK+22
]
for
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
.

However, rather than postulating an uninterpreted parametric left adjoint of
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
as in
[
GCK+22
]
, we can use our knowledge about how this left adjoint is defined semantically to give more specific rules.
Specifically, we can identify its domain as the subcategory of contexts in the essential image of
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
, and on that subcategory the left adjoint actually coincides with
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
.
To represent this semantically, we say that an
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
-context is
flat
if, intuitively, it contains a
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
which is not to the left of any
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
.
Formally, flatness is a predicate on contexts (an additional sort of the GAT) characterised by the following rules:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}}{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}})\;\mathsf{flat}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{flat}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})\;\mathsf{flat}}

Semantically, we think of these as the
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
-contexts that are empty above dimension
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}>{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}
, on which the parametric left adjoint of
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
will act as
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
.
(In our actual model we will do something more clever to avoid assuming the existence of strict initial objects.)

\triangleleft

2.2.2
Substitutions

The judgment
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
says that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}
is a substitution from context
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
to context
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
at mode
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
.
It is generated by the following generating rules, which are the same as those given for MTT in
[
GKNB21
]

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}{{[\;]}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{\mathord{\uparrow}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}~]}{[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}{[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}~]:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\right)\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\right)}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}}{\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\nu}\right)\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\right)}

With the the exceptional rule
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}
, which represents the fact that semantically
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}}
acts as the identity on flat contexts:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{flat}}{\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}\right)}

In practice, it is useful to iterate the weakening rule and combine it with the lock and key rules to obtain the following rule:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\leq\mathsf{locks}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})}{[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta},~\mathord{\uparrow}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}~]:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\right)\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\right)}

In fact, we will generally use named variables and leave weakening implicit.

\triangleleft

2.2.3
Types

These are defined by several classes of type formers, including, at the
most basic level:
\Pi
-types
(parametrised by a modality, as in MTT),
universes
(at each mode), and
modal operators
.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}2}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}2}}}\\
\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\;\mathsf{level}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Disc}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!\;\!\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lsuc}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\;\mathsf{level}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lsuc}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\\
\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

We don’t bother with primitive modal operators
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}
or
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}
, since they can be obtained up to isomorphism by composing the others.

We will work with Tarski style universes, and thus require a decoding
operation:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Disc}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

Finally, we also have types that arise from substitution:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~]\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

As usual, substitution will be
‘eliminable’
in that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~]
is always equal to something not involving
[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~]
, but in the GAT presentation it is one of the generating rules like the others.

\triangleleft

2.2.4
Terms

Terms are defined for each class of type former through introduction
and elimination rules. But first, we have variables.
There are two rules for variables: the ordinary one from MTT, and an
‘exceptional’
one arising, like the exceptional key
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}
, from the fact that
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}
acts as the identity on flat contexts.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\leq\mathsf{locks}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta})}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\mathord{\uparrow}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}~]}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{flat}\quad\mathsf{locks}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta})={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\mathord{\uparrow}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}~]~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]}

For
\Pi
-types, we have (as in MTT):

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}.~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~]}

For universes, we have a coding function:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Code}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Disc}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Code}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

For the modal operators, we have an introduction rule and negative
‘Fitch-style’

elimination rules.
Following
[
GCK+22
]
, we formulate these using parametric adjoints in the mode theory.
As noted in
section

2.1
, the safe modalities have actual left adjoints, so their rules simplify as in
[
Shu23
]
.
And for
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
, we have observed that its parametric left adjoint is defined on the flat contexts, and on those it coincides with
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}\\
\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\blacksquare}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\blacktriangle}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{flat}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\blacklozenge}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]}

Finally, we have terms that arise from substitution:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~]:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~]}

[formula]

2.3

T
elescopes and meta-abstractions, I

2.3.1
Telescopes

Telescopes are suffixes of contexts, with the restriction that they may not contain locks.
The judgement
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
denotes that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
is a telescope in context
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
of ‘level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
’, where the latter means that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
is greater than or equal to the level of the types occurring in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
.
We allow it to be strictly greater, and in particular allow an empty telescope to exist at all universe levels, for a reason to be explained in
section

2.6.3
.
Formally, telescopes are an additional level-indexed sort of the GAT, with formation rules saying that there is an empty one and they can be built by concatenating types.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

Just as with ordinary contexts, we regard these rules as generating telescopes
‘inductively’
, although this is not formally the case syntactically.
We thus regard some other operation on telescopes as
‘defined’
when we specify rules for how it computes on these forms.
This is justified in most models, where we do actually define the judgment of telescopes inductively by the above rules.

For example, the premise of the second rule above requires knowing how to extend a context by a telescope.
We write this with a distinctive notation as
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
, from which the reader can infer that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
is a telescope.
Since
\mid
is an operation on contexts, not a constructor of contexts, it computes on the constructors of telescopes:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta})\;\mathsf{ctx}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}))\equiv(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})

We consider the operation
\mid
to be left-associative with the comma.
Thus, for instance, the context
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}
in the rule for extending a telescope by a type means
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}),~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}
.

By a
strict telescope
we mean a telescope without any nontrivially modal variables.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ctx}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\;\mathsf{stel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{stel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)\;\mathsf{stel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

As is evident, we do not distinguish syntactically between general telescopes and strict ones.
That is, we consider strictness to be a mere
property
of a telescope, or alternatively we treat the obvious map from strict telescopes to telescopes as an implicit coercion.

Similarly, we can introduce a ‘lifting’ operation taking a telescope to any higher level.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}}}

As is evident from the notation, we also treat this as an implicit coercion.
Thus, when we define it recursively on the structure of a telescope, the rules look trivial unless we annotate them somehow with levels:

{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)

[formula]

2.3.2
Partial substitutions

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
there is a judgment
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
for the
‘elements’
of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
.
We call such
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}
a ‘partial substitution’, thinking of it as a substitution
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})
that is the identity on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
.
Formally, we specify that they can be built out of terms:

\frac{\ }{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}~{[\;]}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}~:{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}~]}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)}

The second rule involves a notion of extending an ordinary substitution by a partial one.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~]}{[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\mid{[\;]}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}~]\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\mid[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]~]\equiv[~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~],~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]

This gives a simple way to ensure that partial substitutions are uniquely determined by their components: their equality is detected by equality of the induced substitutions.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\quad[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}~]:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\Rightarrow_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\right)}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}

Note that a partial substitution
does
, in fact,
have

‘components’
: given
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)
we have

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}~]:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu})\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu})

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}~]:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}

We also have a notion of weakening for telescopes. As before, we omit the equations that this must satisfy.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{\mathord{\uparrow}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta})\Rightarrow{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}\mathord{\uparrow}^{{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mathord{\uparrow}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}\equiv\mathord{\uparrow}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\circ\mathord{\uparrow}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}

[formula]

2.3.3
Meta-abstracted types and terms

We now introduce a new judgement form
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.
, where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}
.
This should be thought of saying that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
is a type depending on the variables
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}
in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
, i.e. belonging to a
‘framework-level
\Pi
-type’

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}
.
Accordingly, elements of this judgment are introduced by binding and eliminated by application, with a
\beta
and
\eta
-rule.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\right)\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{422286}{313481}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{356598}{223915}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{422286}{313481}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{356598}{223915}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0 

We also regard
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.
as standing in for its own
\Pi
-type
‘
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}
’
.
Thus, such an
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}
can have its own terms belonging to it, which are also introduced by binding and eliminated by application, with a
\beta
and
\eta
-rule.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\right)\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.59721pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.59721pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}_{\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}:\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{422286}{313481}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{356598}{223915}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{422286}{313481}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{356598}{223915}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{t}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{t}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~:~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\right)\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[ [formula]

2.4

D
écalage and displayed types

Semantically, the fundamental operation is shifting the dimensions of a simplicial type.
In classical simplicial homotopy theory, this is called
décalage
:

\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\right)_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

The simplicial structure maps of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
are a subset of those of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
, while the unused ones assemble into a simplicial map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
.
When
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
is a type at mode
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
, we will regard
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
as the projection from a type
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
dependent on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
; thus we have

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}=({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})

(Semantically, this is validated by the fact that if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
is Reedy fibrant, then the map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
is a Reedy fibration.)
These dependent types
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
, which we call
display
, are our version of the
‘logical relations’
assigned to every type by an internal parametricity theory.

2.4.1
Display for types

In contrast to fully internal parametricity theories, because we don’t have degeneracies in our cube category, décalage and display can only be applied in restricted contexts.
In external parametricity, the logical relations apply only to types in the empty context; but our modalities allow us to say more generally that they apply to any
‘boxed’
type.
Here by
‘box’
we mean not
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
but the corresponding
endofunctor
of the simplicial mode, namely
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}
.
Thus, informally display should have the type
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
, with computability witnesses being assigned by a function
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
.
If we reformulate these without referring to
\Pi
-types, we obtain the following rules for our basic notion of
displayed type
:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]\big)}

However, in order to compute with this, we need a version of it that incorporates dependence on a telescope to the right of the lock.
The corresponding action on that telescope is called décalage.

\triangleleft

2.4.2
Telescope décalage

As noted above, with display
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
defined as dependent on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
, décalage
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
is naturally not a single type but a telescope.
It is therefore natural to generalise its
input
to be a telescope also.
This yields an operation that doubles the variables and groups each type with its displayed version, e.g.

({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}).

The classical projection from décalage to the identity, composed of the leftover face maps, becomes an
‘evens’
substitution
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
that throws away the elements of the displayed types (the primed variables in the above example).
(The corresponding ‘odds’ substitution must wait until we introduce telescope display in
section

2.6.3
.)

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}\\
\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}\;\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]

Notationally, we put a superscript ‘
+
’ on variables and metavariables belonging to décalaged telescopes, and a prime on variables belonging to displayed types and telescopes.
These symbols are part of the variable name, e.g.
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}
above is a single variable that just happens to be named mnemonically.

At this point we can assert that décalage preserves empty telescopes.

{\left(\right)}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{[\;]}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\equiv{[\;]}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{[\;]}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\equiv{[\;]}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

Décalage will also compute on telescopes extended by a type, but we wait to give these rules in
section

2.4.4
, since they require more structure.

\triangleleft

2.4.3
Display for meta-abstractions

The more general version of display alluded to above can informally be thought of as having the following rule:

\text{{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\textquestiondown}}\quad\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\quad{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}?}

However, this is not a well-behaved rule because the context of the conclusion is not fully general.
There are multiple ways to solve this problem; we will solve it by saying that general display acts on a meta-abstracted type.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\;[\;\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}\;]\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}}\right.}\\
\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{t}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{t}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}:\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{858950}{720242}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{858950}{720242}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.75pt}{\resizebox{781401}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.25pt}{\resizebox{871609}{547300}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{t}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\right)~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{858950}{720242}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{858950}{720242}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.75pt}{\resizebox{781401}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.25pt}{\resizebox{871609}{547300}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}}

In general, this does not reduce to ordinary display, but it does when applied to a
décalaged
partial substitution.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma})~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{t}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{A}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{t}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}}

In particular, when
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
these rules say that display for trivial meta-abstractions is equivalent to ordinary display.

\triangleleft

2.4.4
Computing décalage

Now we can give the rules
‘defining’
telescope décalage on telescopes extended by a variable.
Specifically, when extending by a non-modal variable, we also extend by its displayed version.
But that displayed version needs to depend on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
, so we define it in terms of display for meta-abstractions.
Note that the well-typedness of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
in these rules depends on the reduction of meta-abstraction display on displayed partial substitutions.

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}~],~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x^{\prime}}:\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{422286}{313481}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{356598}{223915}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{422286}{313481}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{356598}{223915}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\big)

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~]

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}{{}^{\prime}}~]{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]

The case of a nontrivially modal variable is actually simpler.
Note that in this case, the modality must be of the form
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}
.
Recalling that semantically,
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
constructs a constant simplicial type, we should have informally
({{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}={{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
, and therefore
({{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
is trivial.
For an action on types, this would mean that
({{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
is the unit type; for our current action on telescopes, it means we can just omit the displayed variables.

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}~]\big)

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]

\triangleleft

2.4.5
Computing display

Recall from
section

1
that we treat display computationally like the identity types of HOTT, so that it computes on the basic type-formers.
Note that the abstracting telescope changes as we compute, so these rules could not be stated for ordinary display alone.

2.4.5.1
Non-modal
\Pi
-Types

This rule represents the traditional behavior of parametricity and logical relations on functions: a computability witness for a function says that it preserves computability witnesses.

\displaystyle\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{937888}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\big)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{937888}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{937888}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{1059392}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.0pt}{\resizebox{1252441}{786432}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

2.4.5.2
Nontrivially modal
\Pi
-Types

As with décalage, here we use the fact that display of
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
is trivial.
Note also that here a modal variable appears in the domain of a meta-abstraction.
This is the reason that we cannot restrict to strict telescopes in general.

Universes

2.5

T
elescopes and meta-abstractions, II

The rules given so far essentially suffice to characterise the basic theory of dTT.
However, in order to formulate our definition of semi-simplicial types, we need a bit more structure.
To this end, in this section we introduce some more operations on telescopes that can be
‘defined’
in terms of those already given.

2.5.1
Meta-abstracted telescopes

We start with another judgement form
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\left.\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.
for a telescope dependent on a telescope, with rules entirely analogous to those for types and terms in
section

2.3.3
.
