2.5.2
Telescope concatenation

Telescope concatenation is not necessary for the syntactic definition of SSTs, but seems to be required for a clean description of the semantics.
It is essentially a
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-type for telescopes, which is definitionally associative with context and telescope extension.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}~]:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}~]_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}~]_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~]\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}))\equiv(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right))\equiv(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})

Note that to be at the right universe level, in the rule
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
, the right-hand side ‘
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
’ must be implicitly lifted to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}
.

\triangleleft

2.5.3
\Pi
-telescopes

To define the copointed endofunctors whose coalgebras are display inductive types, we will need
\Pi
-telescopes.
For simplicity, we require that the codomain be a strict telescope; this suffices for our application.
The basic rules are just like those for
\Pi
-types.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{stel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{stel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}.~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}.~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:({\color[rgb]{0,0 In addition, we assert computation laws for
\Pi
-telescopes when the domain or codomain is an extension.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;\mathsf{stel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\xi}:{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta})\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}\\

When telescopes are definitionally lists of types, these rules suffice to compute any
\Pi
-telescope in terms of
\Pi
-types.
Note that in the rule
(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\xi}:{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta})\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
, the ‘
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
’ on the right-hand side must be implicitly lifted to the maximum of the levels of
{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
.

\triangleleft

2.6

D
isplayed telescopes

The structure in
section

2.4
, with display acting on types and décalage on telescopes, is sufficient to determine the behavior of display.
However, in practice we will also need a notion of dependent décalage and display for telescopes.
When telescopes are lists of types, this is determined (like ordinary décalage) by display for types.

2.6.1
Meta-abstracted décalage

Remark 2.4
.

The rules for telescope décalage from
section

2.4.2
and this section should be compared with the
‘local theory’
from
[
ACKS24
]
, with telescopes and telescope concatenation replacing types and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types.
The
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
from
section

2.4.2
corresponds to their
\forall{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
, while the

\triangleleft

2.6.2
Computing meta-abstracted décalage

Like ordinary décalage, meta-abstracted décalage computes on telescopes that are made out of types.
For brevity we omit the typing premises of these equalities, but we emphasize that all the meta-variables on the left-hand sides such as
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}
can depend nontrivially on the abstraction variables
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}
or
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}
.

\displaystyle\quad\quad\ \;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}~]\;\mathchoice{\raisebox{-3.99998pt}{\resizebox{937886}{786431}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.99998pt}{\resizebox{937886}{786431}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.99998pt}{\resizebox{1059390}{786431}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-3.99998pt}{\resizebox{1252440}{786431}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}

\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.59721pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.59721pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}_{\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.59721pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.59721pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}_{\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}

\triangleleft

2.6.3
Telescope display

We also need a notion of indexed display for telescopes.
Note that this always gives a
strict
telescope, even if its input is not.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma})\;\mathsf{stel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]))}

Like décalage, telescope display computes on empty telescopes, and on telescopes extended by a type:

\displaystyle{\left(\right)}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}~{[\;]}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

\displaystyle{[\;]}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

\displaystyle\equiv{[\;]}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]

\displaystyle\equiv\mathrlap{\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x^{\prime}}:\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{422286}{313481}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{356598}{223915}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{534073}{447828}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{422286}{313481}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{0.0pt}{\resizebox{356598}{223915}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}{{}^{\prime}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\right)}

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~]

(for a non-modal variable)

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

(for a modal variable)

As promised, this is the reason that the empty telescope must exist at all levels: if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
consists only of modal variables, then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
is empty, but it must be at the same level as
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
.

Note that compared to décalage, telescope display reorders the variables.
For instance, we have

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y})

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.94444pt}{\resizebox{854608}{716601}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.94444pt}{\resizebox{854608}{716601}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.3611pt}{\resizebox{791209}{587349}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.97221pt}{\resizebox{894801}{561863}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.94444pt}{\resizebox{854608}{716601}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.94444pt}{\resizebox{854608}{716601}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.3611pt}{\resizebox{791209}{587349}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.97221pt}{\resizebox{894801}{561863}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B})\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y})

\displaystyle\not\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}.

Thus, we instead relate telescope display to décalage by an
‘odds’
operation that picks out the elements of displayed types, and a
‘pairing’
operation that interleaves them together, such that evens and odds together form an isomorphism with pairing as inverse.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}od}}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\prime}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}\\
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}od}}}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\prime}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\prime}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}od}}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\prime}}\\

2.6.4
Meta-abstracted telescope display

Unsurprisingly, we generalise telescope display to apply to meta-abstracted telescopes as well, with rules combining those of
sections

2.4.3
and
2.6.3
.

2.6.6
Computing display on
\Pi
-telescopes

Finally, we give the following rules for computing display and meta-abstracted display of a
\Pi
-telescope.
These are consistent with the rules for computing display on telescopes extended by a type.

\displaystyle(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}})

}{\resizebox{923794}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\;:\;({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}})\;\to\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}}\end{multlined}

However, it does not seem possible to give rules for computing
décalage
on a
\Pi
-telescope that are similarly consistent.
Fortunately, we will not need such rules.
Of course, since décalage and
\Pi
-telescopes both compute independently on telescopes extended by a type, so does their combination.

This concludes our description of the ambient syntax of dTT.

\triangleleft

3

Semi-Simplicial and Displayed Coinductive Types

Recall from the introduction that our primary goal in formulating dTT (at the moment) is to have a type theory in which we can make precise our coinductive definition of the type
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
of semi-simplicial types.
In this section we give that definition, making use of the
‘display’
primitives of dTT that was introduced in
section

2
.
The basic definition is contained in
section

3.1
, followed by an exploration of some examples in
section

3.2
.
Then in
section

3.3
we describe a more general notion of
‘displayed coinductive type’
that has
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
as a special case, and in
section

3.4
we explore a few other examples of the general notion.

3.1

S
emi-simplicial types

In an ideal version of displayed type theory, one could define semi-simplicial types as an instance of a general
codata
decleration. We would expect to write this in a proof assistant with a syntax like the following, which generalises Agda-like syntax for records by allowing the coinductive input of each destructor to be specified explicitly and referred to in its type:

⬇

codata

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}

where

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}

It is beyond the scope of this paper to give a sufficiently broad framework to generally encompass such definitions, but we will describe one general paradigmatic class of them, analogous to W-types as paradigmatic inductive types and M-types as paradigmatic coinductive types.
However, we begin by discussing the concrete example of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
in more detail, to help motivate the general case.

3.1.1
SST basics

We begin by giving the type formation law and destructors.
Of course, since
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
is a sort of
‘universe’
, its elements consisting of types, it must also be parametrized by a level.

corresponding to a simple class of syntactic tricks as above. If dTT were extended to have
symmetries

indices and imposing the definitional equality
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}?_{\mathsf{S}_{3}}}
as a corecursor premise. On the other hand, without the ability to line up the two

is well-typed would depend on checking a definitional equality with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}
is well-typed. Since, for the present, we have chosen to develop a theory without symmetries, we must abandon this approach.

as a stuck form in the theory, but will specify how to compute
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
on this normal form. The main idea is that if we define:

⬇

Note that these computation rules were exactly obtained by applying display to both sides of the equation in the initial computation rules. We can iterate this to obtain:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{d}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\big(\big(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{R}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}}}\big)^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{d}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\big)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{d}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{d}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\big(\big(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{R}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}}}\big)^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{d}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\big)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}

\displaystyle\equiv\big(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{R}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}}}\big)^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{d}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{D}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}

The situation on our hands is not unlike that of
Agda
, where a definition of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}
made by (co)pattern matching defines a new normal form and does not expand to a first class intro or elim form when normalised
6
6

6

The culprit here is not a lack of first-class forms, since
Agda
has pattern matching lambdas. Rather, the restriction is made primarily to control such runaway unfolding that would substantially affect the performance of type-checking and normalisation. As a consequence, two structurally identical top-level definitions of functions
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}
made by pattern matching are not definitionally equal.
; such names only reduce when their defining patterns occur. This specific point does not itself inhibit
Nat
canonicity (which
Cubical Agda
otherwise currently lacks due to its treatment of transport in indexed inductives).

We conjecture that dTT, including its treatment of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
, is fully computational in the sense of
Nat
canonicity, normalization, and decidable typechecking.
More precisely, although this may very well not hold
verbatim
of the theory as written down in this paper, we expect it to hold of a modified presentation fitting within the general framework of ideas.
In particular, while we have presented dTT only as a Generalised Algebraic Theory, all the equations have a clear direction and there are no obvious stuck terms.

\triangleleft

3.2

E
xamples of semi-simplicial types

Of course, simply
defining
a type of semi-simplicial types is only the first step: we also want to be able to work with such things conveniently.
Developing a full theory of semi-simplicial types is beyond the scope of this paper, but in this section we will give a few examples to suggest that this at least may be possible with our definition of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
and its corecursion principle.
We will use Agda-esque copattern-matching, and assume that our type theory has plenty of other structure rather than the bare-bones version of dTT that we have studied formally in this paper.

3.2.1
The singular semi-simplicial types

Thus far we have not discussed propositional equality at all, and the reason for this is that the implementation of display is independent from any implementation of equality, whether that be Martin-Löf, cubical, or observational. However, we now want to define a semi-simplicial type that arises from the
\infty
-groupoid structure of a type in HoTT.
For concreteness we will do this using a cubical notion of equality, with notation that aligns with
Cubical Agda
.

When dTT is combined with cubical type theory, we expect display on cubical path types should work as follows.
We have:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Path}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}P}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}P}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\;\;\;\!

3.2.2
Nerves of categories

The semi-simplicial nerve of a 1-category can also be defined by corecursion.
Let
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Cat}}
denote the type of 1-categories, defined as a record inside dTT (extended by record types), and recall that in
section

1
we computed
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Cat}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
to consist of
‘displayed categories’
in the usual sense
[
AL19
]
.
Thus we can define:

⬇

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Nerve}}

:

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Cat}}

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Nerve}}

\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
)

=

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{ob}}

\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Nerve}}

\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
)

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

=

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Nerve}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{coslice}}

\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
)

Here for a category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
and object
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\;\mathsf{ob}}~\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
, by
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{coslice}}~\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
we mean the coslice category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}/\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
, regarded as a displayed category over
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
via the forgetful functor.
Note that a definition of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{coslice}}:\left(\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Cat}}\right)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{ob}}~\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Cat}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
at the global level in dTT automatically induces the definition of the dependent coslice
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{coslice}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
. A similar idea works for bicategories, and any other kind of category for which we can define a displayed (co)slice.

\triangleleft

3.2.3
Topological singular complexes

In
section

3.2.1
we constructed the singular semi-simplicial type associated to the intrinsic
\infty
-groupoid structure of any type.
But we can also construct a more classical singular semi-simplicial set associated to a topological space.
For any type
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Top}}
of
‘topological space’
definable inside of dTT as a record, we have a displayed version
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Top}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
.
In some cases, particularly
‘nonalgebraic’
ones such as open-set spaces, an element of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Top}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
is more general than an
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Top}}
with a map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
; but at least
from
such a
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
we can construct its fibers as a displayed space.
Thus, as long as we can construct, for any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
, a space of
‘continuous paths in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
starting at
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
’
with an endpoint projection down to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
, we can make it a displayed space
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{paths}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
, and use this to construct the singular semi-simplicial types:

⬇

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Sing}}

:

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Top}}

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Sing}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
)

=

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{pt}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Sing}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
)

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

=

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Sing}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{paths}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
)

3.2.4
Fibers and higher spans

As we will see in
section

4
, semantically
each
type at mode
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
is already an augmented semi-simplicial type.
We expect that if we fix a particular
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}})
-simplex in an augmented semi-simplicial type, we should obtain an (unaugmented) semi-simplicial type as its
‘fibre’
.
And indeed, we can define this operation:

⬇

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}

:

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

:
{}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}
)

(

:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
)

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

)

=

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

)

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

=

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

Note that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
is required to be modal so that we can take display of it.
Then we have, for instance, if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}}
,

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}})

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}}

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 000$}}})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 011$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 101$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 110$}}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 000$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 011$}}})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 101$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 110$}}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 000$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 011$}}})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 101$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 110$}}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 000$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 011$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 101$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 110$}}}.

In particular, if we let
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}=\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
be a universe and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top}
be a unit type, we have

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle\cong\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dd}}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}

\displaystyle\cong{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 011$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 101$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 110$}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ddd}}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 011$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 101$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 110$}}}

\displaystyle\cong\begin{aligned} &({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 011$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 011$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}})\\
&({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 101$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 101$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 001$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 110$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 110$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 010$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 100$}}})\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\end{aligned}

Thus
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\top}
is the semi-simplicial type of types, spans, and a sort of simplicial
‘higher spans’
that could also be called
‘heterogeneous simplices’
.
More generally,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}}~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
for any type
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
consists of types, spans, and simplicial higher spans indexed by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
.

\triangleleft

3.2.5
Operations on semi-simplicial types

We can also use corecursion to define operations on semi-simplicial types that are essentially levelwise.
For instance, any two semi-simplicial types have a product:

⬇

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\_\!\times\!\_}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

However, there are some things we would naturally expect to be able to define that do not seem possible with our current theory.
For example, the disjoint union of semi-simplicial types should certainly have the disjoint union of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
-simplices, but the slice over a 0-simplex should come only from one of the two sides.
That is,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y})~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{inl}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
should be morally just
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
.
However,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
belongs to
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
, whereas
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y})~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{inl}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
must belong to
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y})
; thus we need to take its disjoint union with an empty semi-simplicial type displayed over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
.

We defined a
‘global’
empty semi-simplicial type above, and it seems intuitively that we should be able to define a
‘constant’
version of this displayed over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
.
But as noted in
section

3.1
, without symmetry it does not seem possible to formulate a useful corecursor for
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
, and without such a thing it is unclear how to define
‘constantly displayed’
semi-simplicial types.
This suggests that further work in this direction might require the addition of symmetries.

\triangleleft

3.3

D
isplayed coinductive types

Generalizing the discussion of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
, we now formulate a fairly general notion of
‘indexed displayed coinductive type’
.
It depends on a telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
of
‘non-uniform parameters’
, and every element of it has a
‘head’
belonging to some specified type family
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
and a
‘tail’
, depending on a telescope of parameters
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}
, and belonging to the displayed version of the coinductive type itself. The parameters of this displayed version of the very type being defined are
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
, which we can assemble provided that the data of the old parameters
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
, the head
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}
, and the new dependencies
\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}
, are sufficient to extract a section
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}
. The idea is analogous to an
‘indexed M-type’
, but with the output of the tail being displayed, and with
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}
being a telescope rather than a simple type. The pseudo-
Agda
corresponding to this would be:

⬇

module

_

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}

:
{}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}

(

Note that the universe level of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}
is governed by those of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
and
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}
, but does not depend on the level of the telescope of non-uniform parameters
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
.

Following the example of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
, we will begin by attempting to write down a reasonable template for a coinduction principle. In the same module context, we can attempt to map into a

Thus there is a non-trivial condition that needs to be imposed for this definition template to be well typed. Fortunately, unlike in the case of

terms align, which avoids the vicious cycle from before. We get the following rule:

This comes with the following computation rules:

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{h}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
as a particular instance of an indexed displayed coinductive type (which happens to have trivial indexing).
In fact, it is in some sense the
universal

indexed by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}
indexed by
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
.
This may be compared with the fact that the
W

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}
is the type of
‘presentations of well-founded sets’

[
Acz78
]
, while its

‘presentations of ill-founded sets’

[

.

The problem of giving a corecursion rule for
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
carries over to the general case in the following way.
Just as
d
of a
\Pi
-type is another
\Pi
-type and so on for records and ordinary coinductive types,
We’d like to compute
d
of a
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}
to be another
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}
, with something like the following:

\text{{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\textquestiondown}}\quad\begin{multlined}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}_{\;[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},\;\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}~\Big[\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}_{\;[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},\;\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\right),\\
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.75pt}{\resizebox{825543}{612836}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.25pt}{\resizebox{923794}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}head}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}\right)~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.75pt}{\resizebox{825543}{612836}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.25pt}{\resizebox{923794}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}},~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.75pt}{\resizebox{825543}{612836}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.25pt}{\resizebox{923794}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}head}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.75pt}{\resizebox{825543}{612836}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.25pt}{\resizebox{923794}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}},\\
\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.59721pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~[~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}head}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}~]~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+},~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tail}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}~\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.59721pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}_{\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}},\;\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}\Big]\end{multlined}\quad{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}?}

To see whether this is well-typed, observe that we have

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}~]

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}~]~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}

whereas the
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}
of the resulting
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}
must lie in
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}_{\;[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},\;\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
.
Thus, in particular, we need to compare
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}
to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}
, where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\varphi}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
.
In the case of a one-type telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}=\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)
, this becomes

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}~]

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime\prime\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime\prime}}\right)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}~]

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime\prime\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}\right)

Unfortunately the last two are
not
the same!
This is not just about ordering the variables in a telescope; although the second and third arguments of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
both lie in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}
, it need not be symmetrical with respect to those arguments.
So again we see that without adding symmetry to the theory, it seems we can’t give a general corecursor for
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
, and hence we can’t compute
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}corec}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
to something more primitive.

\triangleleft

3.4

E
xamples of displayed coinductive types

We now continue our exploration of the theory of semi-simplicial types from
section

3.2
, now using the general notion of displayed coinductive type.
As in
section

3.2
, we will use Agda-esque codata and copattern-matching definitions, and assume that our type theory has plenty of other structure.

We have already noted that
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
is in some sense the
‘universal’
(unparametrised) displayed coinductive type, whose determining family
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\vdash\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}2}}
is the universal one
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
.
Moreover, it seems likely that in order for an unparametrised displayed coinductive type to be interesting, the types
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
and
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}
must have nontrivial display structure, i.e. they must not be discrete.
But the simplicial universe
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
is the primary source of types with nontrivial display, just as the universe in homotopy type theory is a primary source of types with higher homotopy structure.
(In
5.0.0.9
we will speculate about a notion of
‘display inductive type’
analogous to higher inductive types, which are the other source of higher homotopy structure in homotopy type theory.)
For these reasons, we do not have a lot of interesting examples of other
unparametrised
displayed coinductive types, but there is at least one: augmented semi-simplicial types.

3.4.1
Augmented semi-simplicial types

If we simply omit the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}
input of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}
in the definition of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
, we obtain a definition of
augmented
semi-simplicial types.
(Recall from
section

1
that these are equivalently
unary semi-cubical types
.)

⬇

codata

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ASST}}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}

where

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ASST}}

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}

:

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ASST}}
)

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ASST}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}

We can convince ourselves of this by extracting types of low-dimensional simplices from an
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ASST}}

\displaystyle\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}}

\displaystyle\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}$}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X})

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}00}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}00}$}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}10}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}00}$}}

\displaystyle\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}00}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}10}$}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}))~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}00}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}10}$}}

Now we can observe that the construction

⬇

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}^{\prime}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

:

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
)

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}^{\prime}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
)

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
)

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}^{\prime}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
)

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Fib}^{\prime}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

3.4.2
Pointed semi-simplicial types

More interesting examples of displayed coinductive types have nontrivial parametrizations, often involving more semi-simplicial types.
For instance, we can define the structure of a
pointing
on a semi-simplicial type displayed-coinductively:

⬇

codata

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Pt}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
)

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}

where

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Pt}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

\to

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sp}}

:

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Pt}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
)

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Pt}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

(
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
))

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}

We then have, for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Pt}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
,

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}

\displaystyle:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})

\displaystyle:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}))~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sp}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}))

\displaystyle:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}))~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}))~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sp}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}))

and so on.
That is, an element of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Pt}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
equips
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
with a ‘fat point’, i.e. a chosen
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
-simplex
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}
that comes with all of the higher
‘degenerate simplices’
that one would expect to be associated to
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zp}
if it were in a
simplicial
set rather than a semi-simplicial one.

\triangleleft

3.4.3
Morphisms of semi-simplicial types

With a double parametrization, we can define a type of morphisms of semi-simplicial types.

⬇

codata

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Hom}}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
)

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}

where

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zhom}}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Hom}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}

\to

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

\to

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}shom}}

:

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}

:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Hom}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
)

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

:

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
)

\to

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Hom}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
)

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}

(
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}zhom}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
