{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}

As usual, we can unravel this a few steps to see what it looks like.

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zhom}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}
is a function between types of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
-simplices, which we may denote
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
.
At the next dimension we have:

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zhom}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{shom}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\beta_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 11$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{S}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zhom}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}}))~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zhom}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}})

which is to say

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zhom}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{shom}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}10}$}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}$}})~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}10}$}}).

We may denote this function by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
, and go on to extract a function
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}
between types of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}
-simplices and so on.
We expect other basic operations on semi-simplicial types to be internalizable in a similar way.

\triangleleft

4

Semantics

We now discuss the semantics of dTT.
Specifically, we will show that from any model of ordinary dependent type theory with infinite limits, we can construct a model of dTT in which the original model sits as the discrete mode.

Remark 4.1
.

Actually we will not quite model all of dTT as presented in
section

2
: we omit the type-former
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
and its associated introduction and elimination rule.
This is purely for reasons of simplicity and space.
It should be possible to model
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
as well as long as the starting discrete model has a unit type, but we leave the details for the future.
We will, however, still model
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}
-annotated variables and function types such as
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
.

In
section

4.1
we review the semantics of ordinary dependent type theory, introduce some notation, extend this to our calculus of telescopes and meta-abstractions, and define what it means for such a model to have countable infinite limits.
Then in
section

4.2
we construct a model of augmented semi-simplicial Reedy diagrams, starting with any model of dependent type theory having countable infinite limits.
This is essentially an instance of the general inverse diagram models constructed in
[
Shu15
,
KL21
]
, but we give an explicit inductive construction that avoids category-theoretic machinery and builds display and décalage in from the beginning.
In
section

4.3
we add modalities to this model, and then in
section

4.4
we discuss the
general
notion of model of dTT and show that the simplicial model is in fact such.
Finally, in
section

4.5
we construct displayed coinductive types in these models, including the type
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
of semi-simplicial types.

4.1

T
he semantics of dependent type theory

We approach semantics from the perspective of
Categories with Families
(CwF)
[
CCD21
]
. Here we will recount the relevant categorical concepts while providing a translation into language reminiscent of a type theoretic logical framework.

At the most basic level, a category with families is just a category with a terminal object and distinguished substructure of objects and morphisms that behave like
types
and
terms
in a dependent type theory. In the absence of any other structure, the only way in which this behaviour is manifested is through the presence of
substitution
, which categorically corresponds to a choice of definitionally functorial distinguished pullbacks. Here, instead of giving the substructure as a proposition on objects and morphisms, we first give it as presheaves, and then use representability to overlay this structure into the category.

4.1.1
Categories with Families

A ‘CwF with levels’ consists of a category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
, along with a chosen terminal object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
, and equipped with the data of two families of presheaves, indexed by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\;\mathsf{level}
:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}op}}}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Set}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\int}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}op}}}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Set}},

such that for every
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}:\mathsf{ob}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
, there is a chosen representation of the presheaf:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}~\mapsto\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~:~\mathsf{mor}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\;,\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)\right)\times\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\;,\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\right).

[formula]

4.1.2
Notation

The objects of the category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
are called
contexts
and denoted by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
. For
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}:\mathsf{ob}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
we write:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ob}

The empty context
is the chosen terminal object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
, and is denoted by:

{\left(\right)}\;\mathsf{ob}

The morphisms of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
are called
substitutions
and denoted by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}
. For
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:\mathsf{mor}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)
we write:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}

The unique substitution into the empty context is denoted by:

{[\;]}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\to{\left(\right)}

The notations
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ob}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
are examples of
‘absolute’
or
‘context-less’

judgments
.
In the notation of this section, each absolute judgment asserts that some element belongs to some set, such as the set of objects or a hom-set of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
.
Note that a set can be
‘dependent’
on elements of another set, such as the hom-set
\mathsf{mor}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)
depending on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta},\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}:\mathsf{ob}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}}
; and thus elements of one absolute judgment can appear in another absolute judgment, such as
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\;\mathsf{ob}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ob}
.
Operations on sets can be written as rules, such as composition of morphisms:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}}.

Equations between these operations can likewise be written as rules, where we use
\equiv
for equality since it corresponds to definitional equality in syntax:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\circ({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma})\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau})\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}.

The elements of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
are called
types of level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
and denoted by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}
. For
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
we write:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

Similarly, the elements of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
are called
terms
and denoted by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t},\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}
. For
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)
we write:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}

These notations are examples of
‘hypothetical’
or
‘contextual’
judgments.
In the notation of this section, each hypothetical judgment asserts that some element belongs to a value of some
presheaf
, such as
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
or
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
.
The object of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
at which the presheaf is evaluated (in these examples,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
) is written on the left-hand side of the turnstile
\vdash
.
We annotate it with a formal
‘variable’
such as
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}
, and
‘apply’
all the elements appearing on the right-hand side to that element; at the moment this is just a convention of notation.
As with absolute judgments, one presheaf can be dependent on another, such as
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})
depending on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
; and thus the elements of one hypothetical judgment can appear in another hypothetical judgment, such as
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}
where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
.

For a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
, we denote its functorial action on types
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
and terms
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}
by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}
; thus the presheaf actions of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
and
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
can be expressed by rules

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}}

We allow ourselves to write this alternatively by taking the formal variables
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}
more seriously and
‘applying’

to them:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right):{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)

Formally, this is justified by interpretation in the internal type theory of the presheaf category
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Set}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}op}}}}}
.
By virtue of functoriality, for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Omega}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
we have that

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}\right)\right)\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left(\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}\right){\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}\right)\right)\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~\left(\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}\right)

Now let us consider the representation hypothesis.
In categorical notation, for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}:\mathsf{ob}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
we have a representing object
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}:\mathsf{ob}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}

context extension
.
In type-theoretic notation, we denote the context extension by

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ob}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\;\mathsf{ob}}

Note that this is an operation that takes an element of one set (the absolute judgment
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ob}
) and an element of one presheaf (the hypothetical judgment
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
) and produces an element of a set (the absolute judgment
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\;\mathsf{ob}
).
As before, at the moment the
‘variables’

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}
are just a convention of notation.

We then have a family of bijections, natural in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
:

\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\right)\simeq\left(\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~:~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)\times\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)\right)\right)

Note that this says that a substitution into an extended context
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)
is precisely a substitution
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}
into
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
, along with some term
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}
of type
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}
.
By the Yoneda lemma, the left-to-right part of this bijection is determined by setting
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
to
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)
and evaluating at the identity
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)}
.
The first component gives us a substitution
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
, which we call a
fundamental context projection
or
parent map
7
7

From the perspective of type theoretic fibration categories, an alternative approach to semantics from that of CwFs, the role of fundamental context projections is instead played by
fibrations

and denote by:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\rightarrowtriangle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}

So, in particular, in a CwF we have a distinguished pullback of any parent map along an arbitrary morphism, as another parent map, and this choice of pullbacks is definitionally functorial. We will often omit the superscripts from

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\right)\right)\to\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}=[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\circ\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}~]

Finally, when working with hypothetical judgments in an extended context, we can also treat the variables more traditionally.
Instead of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}

In particular, the zero variable
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}
can be written more simply as

4.1.3
\Pi
-Types

All the basic type-forming operations in syntax translate into structure on a CwF.
For instance, a
\Pi
-structure
on a CwF with levels consists of the following structure and properties:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}\\
\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}\\

laws hold:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}~]}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}^{[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}~]}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}\\
\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}^{\;\!\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}\right)\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}

Or, in indexed notation:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}.~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right):{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}.~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~]~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}

And such that the above constructs are stable under substitution, i.e. for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
:

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}

\displaystyle\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\triangleleft

4.1.4
Universes

A
\mathcal{U}
-structure
on a CwF with levels consists of the following structure and properties:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\;\mathsf{level}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lsuc}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Code}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

Such that
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Code}}
and
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}
are mutual inverses:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Code}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Code}}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}

And such that the above constructs are stable under substitution, i.e. for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
:

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Code}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Code}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\triangleleft

4.1.5
Natural models

We recall from
[
Awo18
]
that a CwF can equivalently be described as a
natural model
: a category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
together with an (algebraically) representable natural transformation
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}
of presheaves on
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
.
This amounts to representing the dependency of terms on types in
‘fibered’
rather than
‘indexed’
style, which is different from the usual type-theoretic notation, but it has the advantage that various operations can cleanly be described in terms of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}
.
Similarly, of course, a CwF with levels can be described by a family of representable transformations
{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
.

In particular, like any morphism in a locally cartesian closed category, any such
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}
induces a polynomial endofunctor
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}
of the presheaf category, where for any presheaf (i.e. judgment)
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
, morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X})
(i.e. elements of the presheaf
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X})
) are bijectively related to pairs consisting of a type
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma})
in context
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
and a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
(i.e. an element of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma})
).
In syntax, this is a bidirectional rule, indicating a bijection between the data above and below the lines:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\xi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\xi}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X})}

Thus, for instance,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}})
represents families of types of level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}
indexed by a type of level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}
.
Therefore, formation rules such as those for for
\Pi
-types and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}

are represented by morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}})\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}
.

The rules for terms can also be represented in this language.
For instance, a natural model has
\Pi
-types if and only if there is a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}}

meaning that there is a bijection

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}

Polynomial functors can also be composed, yielding another polynomial functor.
For instance, in a CwF without levels,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}
is the functor such that
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X})
represents elements of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
in a doubly-extended context
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a})
, which means that it is the polynomial functor associated to the map
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}})
where the fiber of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma})
over
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B})
consists of a pair of terms
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}
.
In particular, a CwF
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
has
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types if and only if
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}})\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}
represents any such pair by a single term, i.e. there is a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}}

This is equivalent to a (cartesian) morphism of polynomial functors
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}
.
Of course, there is an analogous version for a CwF with levels.

\triangleleft

4.1.6
Telescopes

We will often have finite towers of types:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}2}}

We represent these with a single judgement, defining a
telescope
:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}.

Formally speaking, telescopes and their elements (which we call
partial substitutions
) are another CwF structure on the same category of contexts, which are related to the original one by specified operations.
In natural model style, the definition is:

Definition 4.5
.

A natural model with levels
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}

has telescopes
if it is equipped with:

•

Another family of (algebraically) representable natural transformations
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
.
This yields two families of judgments for telescopes and partial substitutions:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}

Their representability yields the extension of a context by a telescope:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ob}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma})\;\mathsf{ob}.}

•

Morphisms of polynomial functors
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}
, i.e. pullback squares

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}.}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\left(\right)}}

This gives ‘empty telescopes’
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\left(\right)}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
containing exactly one partial substitution
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{[\;]}:{\left(\right)}
.

•

Morphisms of polynomial functors
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}
whenever
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
.
This says how to extend a telescope by a type:

Note that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}}
is the polynomial functor associated to a map whose codomain is
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}})
, which is the presheaf of types in a context extended by a telescope.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}{{}^{\prime}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

such that the partial substitutions in
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})
are exactly pairs of a partial substitution in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
and a term in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
, just as for
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types.
Thus we get the rules from
section

2.3.2
.

•

The rules
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
and
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}))\equiv(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})

Note that these are equalities of objects of

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}

•

A morphism of polynomial functors
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}}
, giving the extension of telescopes by telescopes
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})
from

2.5.2
, such that the rules from that section hold:

({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}))\equiv(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\left(\right)})\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right))\equiv(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}),{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})

Syntactically, this definition represents the rules from
sections

2.3.1
,
2.3.2
and
2.5.2
, in the non-modal case.
Because it is phrased in terms of presheaves and operations on them, it implicitly includes substitution into telescopes that commute with the other operations.
Some of these commutation properties refer to weakening-two, which can be characterised in terms of them as well, for instance:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)\right)\to\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)}\\
{\left(\right)}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\equiv{\left(\right)}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left(\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\right)~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~]\right)\right)\\
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{{\left(\right)}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\right)

For example, we have:

\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~]\right)\right)~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~]\right)\right)

When we allow ourselves to use variables in the usual way, justified by the internal type theory of presheaves, we can write this as:

\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)

Note that the meaning of this construction is simply iterating the canonical construction of pullbacks over a tower:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)\right)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces[~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~\circ~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}~]~\circ~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}~]}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~\circ~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}~]}

Definition 4.6
.

A CwF with levels
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
with telescopes
has
\Pi
