•

There is a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}}

•

The computation rules from
section

2.5.3
hold.

Now the above rules allow us to build telescopes up from the empty telescope by adding types, just as the rules of a CwF allow us to build contexts from the empty context by adding types.
However, just as in the case of contexts, the rules do not stipulate that every telescope is obtained in that way.
Indeed, there is no way to assert such a thing in a Generalised Algebraic Theory.
However, it holds
‘admissibly’
in the initial syntactic model, and any CwF can be extended with telescopes in this way:

Theorem 4.7
.

Any CwF with levels can be equipped with telescopes.
If it has
\Pi
-types, it also has
\Pi
-telescopes.

Proof.

We define
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
to be the map such that

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}=\sum_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{N}}\atop\forall{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}i}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}i}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}}\circ\cdots\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}}}}}.

Thus an element of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma})
is a tower of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
types over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
of level
\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
, and similarly for terms.
The two morphisms of polynomial functors are then immediate.
We define context extension in the obvious way by iterating context extension by types, and the equations hold.
(This is the
initial
structure of telescopes on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}
in a straightforward sense.)
Similarly, we define
\Pi
-telescopes by using the rules for computing them on extended telescopes.
∎

4.1.7
Meta-abstractions

Because meta-abstractions are not
‘reified’
in the theory as types, they do not require assuming any structure beyond that which is already present in the presheaf category.
Specifically, the rules for the judgment
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\left.\;\mathsf{type}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.
simply say that it should be (up to isomorphism) the object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}})
that classifies types indexed by a telescope.
Similarly, the rules for the elements of a meta-abstraction simply say that these are the object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}})
that classifies terms indexed by a telescope.
In other words, meta-abstractions of types and their terms are classified by a map (isomorphic to)
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}})
.
Likewise, meta-abstractions of telescopes (the judgment
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\left.\;\mathsf{tel}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.
) are classified by a map isomorphic to
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}})
.
This gives all the rules from
sections

2.3.3
and
2.5.1
; thus any natural model with telescopes also has meta-abstractions of types and telescopes.

Semantically, we don’t ever need to discuss meta-abstractions explicitly, since to judge
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.
is equivalent to judging
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
, and so on.
Thus we will generally talk only about types and telescopes in contexts.

\triangleleft

4.1.8
Infinite Telescopes

We now define a new judgement
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{stel}^{\infty}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
whose elements are ‘infinite telescopes’.
As with meta-abstractions, this is not (yet) introducing new structure on a CwF, rather it is a definition that can be made in the presheaf category of any CwF.
The idea is that an infinite telescope consists of an infinite sequence of types each dependent on all the previous ones:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}

\displaystyle\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}

\displaystyle\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}

\displaystyle\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}2}}}

where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
for all
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
.
Formally, we define this along with its approximating finite telescopes:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}

\displaystyle\equiv{\left(\right)}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial 1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial 2}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\right)

so that we can say that in general
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
is a type in context
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}})
.
In syntax, this means we give the following bidirectional rule with infinitely many premises:

\frac{\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\in\mathbb{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}N}}}\quad\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\in\mathbb{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}N}}}}\quad({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell})_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\in\mathbb{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}N}}}\quad\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial 0}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\equiv{\left(\right)}\quad\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\in\mathbb{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}N}}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{stel}^{\infty}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}

(It would also be possible to define infinite contexts coinductively, but for our purposes this concrete definition is easier to work with.)

We have already defined substitution on finite telescopes, and that definition extends level-wise to infinite telescopes. Given
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{stel}^{\infty}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
, we define
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)\;\mathsf{stel}^{\infty}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
to consist of the data:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}

Similarly, we would like to define infinite partial substitutions as infinite lists of terms sectioning an infinite telescope. This is encapsulated by the judgement
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}
, which is characterised by a similar bidirectional rule:

\frac{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma})_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\in\mathbb{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}N}}}\quad({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}))_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\in\mathbb{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}N}}}\quad\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial 0}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\equiv{[\;]}\quad({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~])_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\in\mathbb{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}N}}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}

Pullback of infinite partial substitutions is defined, as before, to consist of the data:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right):{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\delta}\right)\right)

Categorically, these rules mean we define the map
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
to be the limit of the sequence:

\cdots\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\to\cdots\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}

where
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
is the map such that

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}=\sum_{\forall{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}i}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}i}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}}\circ\cdots\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}}}}}.

In particular,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
is the identity functor and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
is the identity map of the terminal object.
There is only one natural map
{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\to{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, which discards the last type in a telescope of length
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
; it is not possible to discard any of the other types and get a telescope of length
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
.

\triangleleft

4.1.9
\omega
-Limits

Finally, we define the structure of infinite (sequential, Reedy) limits on a CwF.
These are an
‘infinitary rule’
(i.e. a non-elementary structure) that is not part of dTT or any implementable type theory, but we will use them to build our intended models of dTT.
Syntactically, they are essentially just a kind of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-type of an infinite telescope.

Definition 4.8
.

A CwF with levels has
\omega
-limits
if it is equipped with pullback squares

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}}

In syntax, this means we have the following structure and properties.
Firstly, having a merely
commutative
square as above gives the following rules:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{stel}^{\infty}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\big)\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\big):\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\big)}

Secondly,

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\big)}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\big)}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~\big(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}\big)}

We require that
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
is derived from
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
via:

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial 0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}

\displaystyle\equiv{[\;]}

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}},~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}~]

and that the following computation and uniqueness rules hold:

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{a}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\right)

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{a}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{a}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\right)

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{a}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{u}}\right)_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}

Of course, all these constructions must also be stable under substitution:

\displaystyle\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\right)\right)

\displaystyle\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{a}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{a}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\right)\right)

\displaystyle\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{a}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{a}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\right)\right)

\displaystyle\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{a}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{a}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}\right)\right)

\triangleleft

4.2

T
he simplicial model

In this section we fix a model of dependent type theory with all of the structure described above, which we call the
discrete model
(
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}
). From it, we will construct a derived model called the
simplicial model
(
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
). We will do this, first, by way of constructing the
truncated simplicial models
(
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
) for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}2}}}
.

4.2.1
The Augmented Semi-Simplex Category

Let
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}
be the type of binary digits, which are
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}
. For
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}
, let
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
be the type of length
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
binary sequences such that exactly
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
of the digits have value
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
. When
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
, we have a composition
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
obtained by replacing the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
digits in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}
with the digits of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}
. For example
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}
. The category whose objects are
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}
and whose morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}
are
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
is the augmented semi-simplex category
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}}
. Note that each of the representables
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}
only has finitely many elements. We write
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\varnothing}
for the length-zero sequence, which is the unique element of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
.

The identities
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
are given by length
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
sequences of the digit
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
. Further, for any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
, we obtain
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
by left appending the indicated digit. The following identities hold:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\right)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\right)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\right)

Note that by the second rule, along with the fact that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
, the assignments
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}\mapsto{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\mapsto{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}
define an endofunctor of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}}
.

Additionally, for every
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}2}}}
, we have the full subcategory
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}}
on those objects
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}
with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
.
Thus
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}2}}}}
is the empty category, while
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}}}
is the terminal category.

\triangleleft

4.2.2
Truncated Simplicial Objects

The objects of the
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
-truncated simplicial model
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
are
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
-valued presheaves on
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
, denoted:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\;\mathsf{ob}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}

Thus the underlying category of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
is
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathcal{C}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}}
.
For each such presheaf and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}2}}}
, we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}\;\mathsf{ob}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}
, where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}2}}}\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}
is the distinguished terminal object of
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
.

Further, if we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
, then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}
, and this assignment is contravariantly functorial on the nose. We also sometimes write
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}
for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}
. Morphisms of simplicial objects are natural transformations. The data of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
thus consists of a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
for each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, such that for any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
, we have:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}

There are two additional functors of relevance relating the truncated simplicial models at different dimensions:
truncation
and
décalage
.

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}}\to\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}}

\displaystyle\left(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}}\to\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}

There is a natural transformation between them:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}:\left(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\Rightarrow{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}}

Note that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
is a morphism of presheaves since for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{B}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}
, we have:

\displaystyle\big({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\big)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\circ\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\right)}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}\right)}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\big)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}

A similar proof shows that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}
is natural, as its components arise from morphisms in
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
, and any morphism of presheaves must respect these.

\triangleleft

4.2.3
Intuition

We will now construct the type-theoretical/fibrant structure of the truncated simplicial model. This will be done concretely through a series of mutually inductive definitions that will require substantially strengthening the inductive hypothesis for the sake of making everything well-typed.

However, before we launch into that, it would be useful to keep in mind where we are headed. At the most basic level, we would like to define the judgement

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

A simplicial type consists entirely of the data of its discrete
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}
-simplex types for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
, all of which live at the same level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 0$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{0}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\text{}}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 00$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 01$}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle 10$}}}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

Note that

\displaystyle\;\vdots

Similarly to before, we will write this generically as

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}\right)

where
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}
denotes the action of the lower-dimensional parts of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}
on the boundary of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}
.

\triangleleft

4.2.4
Fibrant Structure

As suggested above, the basic structure of the fibrant theory of the models
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
will be defined by mutual induction.
In this section our goal is to define the presheaves of types and terms in
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
, along with the context extension operation (but not yet its universal property).
This requires defining several other notions mutually, including a type-theoretic version of Reedy
‘matching objects’
and a truncated version of display that decreases dimension.

4.2.4.1
Declarations and Simple Cases

We start by declaring the type of all these structures and operations, and giving those definitions that are direct.
First, we will have
matching telescopes
and
matching substitutions
:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}}

The inductive definitions of these telescopes and substitutions will be given in
4.2.4.2
.
However, in terms of them, we are able to define the types and terms of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
, as pairs of a type or term in
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
with a discrete type or term over its matching object.
We can formulate these definitions type-theoretically as bidirectional rules.

\frac{\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\quad\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}\quad\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}\right)}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}

Extension of contexts by a type
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
, and of a substitution by a term
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}
, are then obtained as follows:

\displaystyle\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\equiv\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\quad\text{for}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}<{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}

\displaystyle\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\equiv\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\big)

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\quad\text{for}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}m}<{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~].

So far this is just a definition of the family of discrete
objects
underlying
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)
; we will enhance it to a diagram in (
4.15
) below.

We will also prove that matching telescopes and substitutions are stable under substitution, such that for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}}
, we have:

\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}\equiv\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}\big)^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}\equiv\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}\big)^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}

Substitution on types
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
and terms
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}
can then be defined as:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\big)

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}

\displaystyle\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\big)

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}

\displaystyle\big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\big)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}.

Functoriality of substitutions in
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
then follows from that of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
and
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}
.

In order to define the matching telescopes and substitutions, we will require the definition of
display
to be part of the mutual induction.
As noted above, when working with truncated diagrams, display takes an
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})
-truncated semi-simplicial diagram
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
to an
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
-truncated one that’s dependent
on
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
. Since we have no modal locks available yet, we are also forced to take this version of display to be in a totally décalaged context; recall that décalage makes sense for arbitrary (non-fibrant) contexts.

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}}

We will prove that display is stable under substitution by
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}}
, and satisfies the expected formulas relating it to décalage:

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\right)^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}W}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}}\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\right)^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}

\displaystyle\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\right)

(4.9)

\displaystyle[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}

Given these, we can then define the functorial structure of the putative object
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)
: a morphism

acts on it by:

\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}},~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}act}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}act}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~]

(4.15)

Equations

4.11
and
4.12
tell us that the assignment
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\right)^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}
is functorial, while
eqs.

4.13
and
4.14
tell us that the extension
[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~]
is a morphism of presheaves.

The above is the complete list of constructions and theorems that we need in order to inductively define the type and term presheaves in the models
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
and their context extension function.

4.2.4.2
The Inductive Cases

Now we give the inductive definitions and proofs of the objects and theorems declared previously.
The model
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}2}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}2}}}}
is the terminal CwF on the terminal category. For
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}
, we have that:

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}\right)}\equiv{\left(\right)}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}{\mathchoice{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptstyle-$}1}{\scalebox{0.6}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}1}}}\right)}\equiv{[\;]}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}

from which the rest of the definitions and theorems evidently follow.

Suppose now that the model
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
has been defined with all of the above structure and properties. We first define matching telescopes and substitutions as follows:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+2}}

\displaystyle\equiv\begin{aligned} \Big({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+2}},~&{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+2}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a},\\

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\right)}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+2}}

\displaystyle\equiv[~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)},~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}},~\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\right)_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\right)}~].
