For the parent maps
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}
, we make a definition by cases on whether or not
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
is flat:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv\begin{cases}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}&\text{for}\quad\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\\
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}&\text{for}\quad\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}.\end{cases}

The parent maps for
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
reduce to discrete parent maps of variables of modal type:

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}.

Then, for
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
, we combine this with the substitution above:

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pt}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}.

For the zero variables for
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
, one checks that the following are well-typed:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\blacklozenge}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\blacksquare}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}.

For the zero variables
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}
, we once again case split:

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv\begin{cases}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}&\text{for}\quad\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\\
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}&\text{for}\quad\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}.\end{cases}

Then, for
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
, we use
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}
:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\blacklozenge}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}\equiv{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\blacksquare}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{zv}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}.

\triangleleft

4.3.7
Modal
\Pi
-Types

The last remaining modal construct that we must address is modal
\Pi
-types. These behave according to the following rules:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{{\small\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}{\small\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash_{{\small\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\small\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{{\small\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\small\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\;\sqcup\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\vdash_{{\small\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\small\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{{\small\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\small\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}}\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{{\small\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}{\small\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{]}}}$}}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\quad{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}\vdash_{{\small\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{[}}}$}\kern-1.47914pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0, For
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
we define:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\right)

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\big)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\right)

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}\big)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\right)

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\big)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\right)

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~\big({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}\big)

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{sm}}}~\big(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}\big)

\displaystyle\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~\left(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~\big(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}\big).

The other cases reduce to functions of a modal variable:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}~\left({{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~\left({{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}~\left({{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}~\left({{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\right)~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}

The cases of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lambda}
and
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}app}}
are similar.

\triangleleft

4.4

S
emantics of dTT

Having reviewed the general notion of model for dependent type theory in
section

4.1
, and constructed our intended model of dTT in
sections

4.2
and
4.3
, we now describe the general notion of model for dTT.
Of course, since our syntax was presented as a Generalised Algebraic Theory, there is an immediate notion of
model
, namely an algebra for that theory (with algebraic syntax being the initial model).
The point is to reformulate this in more familiar category-theoretic terms.

4.4.1
Modal structure

The general multimodal type theory MTT was presented algebraically in
[
GKNB21
]
.
We therefore start from this as a baseline and add structure corresponding to our particular theory.

For a general mode 2-category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
, the starting point is a
modal context structure
, which is a 2-functor
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}
, where
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}
denotes reversal of both 1-cells and 2-cells.
The image of a mode
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
is the category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
of contexts and substitutions at that mode, and the image of a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}
is the lock functor
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}\to\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
, which we write postfix,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mapsto{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}
.
It is a
modal natural model
if each
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
is equipped with a morphism
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
in its presheaf category such that for any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}
the morphism
(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu})^{*}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})
is representable.
(In particular, taking
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
, we see that each
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
is an ordinary natural model, hence a CwF.)
This notion encapsulates all the rules for building contexts and substitutions from
section

2.2
except for those that refer to flatness of contexts.

Now, specializing to our mode 2-category from
section

2.1
, the rules of
section

2.2
say that the flat contexts form a full subcategory of
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
that contains the image of
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
.
In our algebraic theory we take as primitive the derived rules that a context is flat if and only if it admits a substitution to
({\left(\right)},\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}})
, and in that case the latter substitution is unique.
Thus, semantically,
1\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
is subterminal and the flat contexts are the slice category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}/1\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
.
Since the unit of the adjunction
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}\dashv\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle}}}
is an identity,
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
is fully faithful, and on its image it has
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
as an inverse and therefore also a left adjoint.
In addition, since flat contexts are fixed points (up to isomorphism) of
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}}
, when
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
is flat there is a bijection
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma})\cong\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}})
, and so the modal comprehension
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\!\lozenge}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})
is isomorphic to an ordinary one
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\prime}})
.
This justifies the special variable rule and key substitution.
Thus, the following definition encapsulates the judgmental structure of our modal type theory.

Definition 4.29
.

A
dTT context structure
is a modal context structure
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}
in the sense of
[
GKNB21
]
, where
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
is as in
section

2.1
, such that
1\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
is subterminal and the slice category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}/1\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
is the replete image of the fully faithful functor
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dm}}}\to\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
.
A
dTT natural model
is a dTT context structure that is also a modal natural model.

Next, since our modalities are Fitch-style, their semantics follows
[
GCK+22
]
.
This requires each functor
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}
to
be
a parametric right adjoint and
have
a dependent right adjoint.
However, since each safe
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}
is already a right adjoint in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
, such
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}}
are also ordinary (hence parametric) right adjoints.
And since
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
is an equivalence onto a slice category, the inverse of that equivalence is a parametric left adjoint of it.
Thus, to justify our Fitch-style rules for modalities, it suffices to assume the following.

Definition 4.30
.

A
dTT modal model
is a dTT natural model such that the functors
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
and
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}}
have dependent right adjoints.

Our primary example is, of course, the following.

Theorem 4.31
.

The simplicial model of
sections

4.2
and
4.3
is a dTT natural model.

Proof.

Of course, we use the extended simplicial model along with the discrete model.
We showed explicitly in
section

4.3
that this yields a modal context structure for our
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
.
In the notation of that section, the object
1\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}}
referred to above is
\left({\left(\right)},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}\right)\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}in_{dm}}}~{\left(\right)}
.
The definition of the category
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
implies immediately that this object is subterminal and its slice category is the replete image (and even the literal image) of
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
.
Finally, in
section

4.3.5
we verified the rules of
[
GCK+22
]
for
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
and
{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
, which as shown in
loc. cit.
are equivalent to their being dependent right adjoints of
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\lozenge}}
and
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
.
∎

4.4.2
Telescopes

Modal telescopes generalise ordinary telescopes to modal natural models in a straightforward way.
Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
be a 2-category.

Definition 4.32
.

A modal natural model
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}

has telescopes
if it is equipped with:

•

For each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\in\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}
, a representable natural transformation
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
, whose comprehensions we write as
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma})
.

•

For each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
, a morphism of polynomial functors
{\left(\right)}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}
.

•

For any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}
, a morphism of polynomial functors
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}^{*}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}pr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}q}}
that we write as
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta})
.

•

The rules
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\left(\right)})={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
and
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}))=(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})
from
section

2.3.1
hold.

•

A morphism of polynomial functors
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}}
, which we write as
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
.
(This says how to concatenate telescopes.)

•

The rules
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}))=(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma})\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})
and
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\left(\right)})={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
and
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}))=(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mu}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi})
from
section

2.5.2
hold.

In addition, we say
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
has
\Pi
-telescopes
if for each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}
there is a pullback square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}P}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tpr}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}p}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Pi}}

such that the computation rules from
section

2.5.3
hold.

As in
sections

4.1.6
and
4.1.7
, we can equip any modal natural model with telescopes and
\Pi
-telescopes, and interpret meta-abstracted types and telescopes automatically, without needing to discuss them explicitly.

\triangleleft

4.4.3
Display and décalage

If
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
is a CwF with telescopes and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\in\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
, we write
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
for the category whose objects are telescopes
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma})
and whose morphisms are morphisms
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1})\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}2})
in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
.
Thus, it is equivalent to the full subcategory of
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
on objects of the form
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
.
We call this
the category of telescopes of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
.
Note that by substitution, it is strictly functorial in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
, i.e. we have a functor
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash-:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}op}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}
.
Equivalently, therefore, we can regard this as an internal category in the presheaf category
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Set}}^{\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}op}}}}}
.

In fact the category
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
is actually itself a CwF.
Its
‘types’
in
‘context’

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
are meta-abstracted telescopes
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\left.\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}\right.
.
These are equivalent (but not equal) to telescopes in an extended context, i.e. the elements of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})
.
Similarly, meta-abstracted partial substitutions
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
are equivalent to terms
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\vdash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}
, and semantically to sections of such a projection,
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})
over
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})
.
Comprehension is by telescope concatenation.
Because
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\left(\right)}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
, the CwF
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
has the following special property.

Definition 4.33
.

A CwF
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
is
strongly democratic
if every context is the comprehension of a unique type in the empty context.

Since all of the structure of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
is strictly stable under substitution in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
, these categories form an internal CwF in the presheaf category
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Set}}^{\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}op}}}}}
.
We call this the
internal telescope model
of
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
and denote it
\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}
.
Recalling
remark

2.4
and comparing to the discussion of the local theory in
[
ACKS24
]
, we find that the syntactic structure of décalage from
sections

2.4.2
and
2.6.1
can be described precisely as an internal CwF morphism.

Definition 4.34
.

Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}
be a dTT natural model with telescopes.
We say it
has décalage
if it is equipped with a strict morphism of internal strongly democratic CwFs

(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}:(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

in the category of presheaves over
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
, together with an internal natural transformation
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}evens}}
from
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
to
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]:(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
.

In particular, therefore, this structure ordinary includes functors

(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}

and natural transformations
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}evens}}
consisting of maps

({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}})\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}),

all strictly stable under pullback.
This, together with the strict preservation of empty contexts by the functor
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
, is what the rules of
section

2.4.2
say.
The corresponding action on
‘types’
(meta-abstracted telescopes) and
‘terms’
(meta-abstracted partial substitutions) assembles into the rules of
section

2.6.1
.

We can phrase display in a similar way by defining an auxiliary internal CwF.
We start with telescope display (
section

2.6
).
Recall from
[
Shu15
,
KL21
]
that from any CwF
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
we can construct a
‘Sierpinski’
model
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}
.
Its objects (contexts) are arbitrary morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
, but its types are pairs of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0})
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\centerdot{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}~])
.
Moreover, there is a strict CwF morphism
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\to\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
, which preserves all the type-formers, in particular
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types if
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
has them.
If
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
has
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types there is also a functor
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\to\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
that sends a type
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})
to
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}~],{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})
, but this only preserves comprehension and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types up to isomorphism.
Thus it is a pseudo CwF morphism in the sense of
[
CD11
, Definition 10]
, although it preserves substitution and the empty context strictly.

Now let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
be a CwF, and apply this construction internally in the category of presheaves on
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
to the internal telescope model
\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}
.
We thus obtain another CwF
\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}
internal to presheaves, in which the
‘contexts’
over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
are morphisms of telescopes
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
, and the
‘types’
in such a
‘context’
over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}
are pairs of two telescopes
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0})
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\theta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}01}~])
.
This is no longer strongly democratic, but as always we have the strict CwF morphism
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}:\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}
that preserves
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types (i.e. telescope concatenation), and the pseudo CwF-morphism
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}:\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}
.
Moreover, in this case the latter is actually a strict CwF-morphism, because telescope concatenation is strictly associative.

Definition 4.35
.

Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}
be a dTT natural model with telescopes.
We say
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}

has telescope display
if it is equipped with

1.

An internal pseudo CwF morphism that preserves substitution, the empty context, and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types strictly:

(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}:(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}

2.

An equality between the composite
(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\xrightarrow{(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\xrightarrow{(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
and the key transformation
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]:(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
.
Since the latter is a strict morphism, that means that so is the former.

3.

A strict internal CwF morphism

(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}:(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

and an isomorphism of pseudo CwF morphisms between
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
and the composite morphism
(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\xrightarrow{(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\xrightarrow{(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}
, that is the identity on underlying functors.

We have not assumed
a priori
in
definition

4.35
that
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
has décalage, but it is actually included: the morphism
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
is of course the same as in
definition

4.34
, and the transformation
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}evens}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
from
definition

4.34
arises in
definition

4.35
as the image of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
under the underlying functor of
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
.
The additional data in
definition

4.35
beyond this is the
1
-part of the action of
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
(the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
-part is determined by the composition with
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
equaling
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]
) making it a pseudo CwF morphism preserving substitution and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types strictly, and the isomorphism on
‘types’
(dependent telescopes) between
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
and the composite of
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
with
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
.
But since the latter is to be a pseudo CwF transformation (see
[
CCD17
, Appendix B]
), and since
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}
is strict and the underlying functor is the identity this just means that this isomorphism must coincide with the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
-part of the comprehension coherence isomorphism of
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
(the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
-part being the identity).

So all that remains is the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
-part of the action of
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
on meta-abstracted telescopes, preserving substitution and telescope concatenation, and coherence isomorphisms relating it to comprehension.
This gives the rules of
section

2.6.4
, which have
section

2.6.3
as a special case.
In particular, since the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
-part of the comprehension of
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}})
in
\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}
is
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}})
, the comprehension isomorphisms are the pairing
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}
together with
ev
and
od
.

Finally, we consider display of types, as in
section

2.4.3
, and its relation to décalage as in
sections

2.4.4
and
2.6.2
.
In some ways this is simpler, since we don’t have to worry about rearranging between display and décalage; but in other ways it is more complicated, since we have to take account of extending dependent telescopes by types.

To start with, note that the internal telescope model
\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}
of any CwF has a
‘sub-model’

\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
whose internal category of
‘contexts’
is the same (telescopes), but whose internal presheaf of
‘types’
consists of the
length-
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
telescopes
, i.e. single types annotated by a modality.
Note that unlike
\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}
, it does not automatically have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Sigma}
-types.

Definition 4.36
.

Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}
be a dTT natural model with telescopes.
We say
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}

has type display
if it is equipped with

1.

An internal strict CwF morphism:

(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}:(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}

2.

An equality between the composite
(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\xrightarrow{(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}\xrightarrow{(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
and the key transformation
(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]:(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}
.

3.

If a length-1 telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
is non-modal, then the telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
is a single non-modal type.

4.

If a length-1 telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
is nontrivially modal, then the telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
is empty.

Note that, like
definition

4.35
, this definition includes décalage.
It represents the rules for display from
sections

2.4.1
and
2.4.3
, and the rules for computing décalage on a telescope extended by a type from
section

2.4.4
.
Of course, with both telescope display and type display we want them to be compatible.

Definition 4.37
.

Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}

We say it has

if the restriction of

(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}:(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\to\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}
to
(\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})^{*}\mathbf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
is an internal strict CwF morphism such that

and

of

•
