2.6.5
for computing meta-abstracted telescope display in terms of type display hold.

Finally, we add the compatibility conditions with type-formers:

Definition 4.38
.

Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}coop}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathcal{C}\!\mathit{at}}
be a dTT natural model with telescopes, décalage, telescope display, and type display.
We say that
display respects
\Pi
-types
(respectively
universes
) if the rules in
section

2.4.5
hold.

This completes the description of the abstract categorical semantics of the theory of
section

2
: it is a dTT natural model with telescopes and complete display that respects
\Pi
-types and universes.
However, as noted in
section

2
, when telescopes are lists of types, as they almost always are, much of this structure can be deduced from the rest.

Theorem 4.39
.

Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
be a dTT natural model, with telescopes defined from types as in
theorem

4.7
, and with type display defined relative to these telescopes.
Then there is a unique way to extend this type display on
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
to complete display.

Proof.

The rules in
section

2.6
for computing telescope display and décalage in terms of type display uniquely determine those operations when telescopes are defined as lists of types.
∎

Using this, we can verify that our intended model is indeed a model.

Theorem 4.40
.

The simplicial model of
sections

4.2
and
4.3
has type display, and hence complete display, which respects
\Pi
-types and universes.

Proof.

We constructed a display operation for the simplicial model in
section

4.2
, but it does not yet have exactly the needed form.
What we have so far is a
‘global’
operation that décalages the whole context:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}\;\mathsf{type}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}}.

(Note that this is only defined on the original simplicial model
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
, not the extended one
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}+}
: indeed, décalage is not even defined on flat contexts.)
But the (meta-abstracted version of the) operation we specified in the syntax of
section

2
is a
‘local’
one that only décalages part of the context, keeping the rest of it modally locked away:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;\mathsf{type}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}}

However, it is straightforward to obtain the latter from the former.
In
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{+}
, a context of the form
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\right)
is not flat, hence lies essentially in
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}
so that décalage is defined on it.
Furthermore, we already observed that
\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}\right)
since
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\square}}
lands in constant presheaves.
Thus, when
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
is a telescope built out of types, we have

\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\right)

and so the global operation yields as a special case

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{+}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;\mathsf{type}}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\rho}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}_{+}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}+}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}\;\mathsf{type}}.

Now we simply substitute along
\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}
to obtain the desired local rule.
The necessary computation rules for décalage,
\Pi
-types, and universes follow immediately from the rules we proved for the global operation in
section

4.2
.
∎

4.4.4
Display of
\omega
-limits

Finally, when we have both display and also
\omega
-limits, it is reasonable to require the former to compute on the latter, in the following way.
Suppose that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;\mathsf{stel}^{\infty}
, and we want to compute
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}\vdash\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}
.
Then by definition, we have

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\left.\;\mathsf{tel}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}}\right.

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}}\right.

and therefore

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\left.\;\mathsf{tel}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}}\right.

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\left.\;\mathsf{type}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}}\right.

Weakening and substituting to the needed context
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}
, we have

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}})\;\mathsf{tel}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}})

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}})\;\mathsf{type}

such that

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}})

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\right){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~[~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}},~\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}}~]

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}}),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}})\right).

Thus, these data form another infinite telescope, which we denote

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}\;\mathsf{stel}^{\infty}

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}})^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}

\displaystyle\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}})

\displaystyle({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}})^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}

\displaystyle\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}})

We say that
display respects
\omega
-limits
if

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}(\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}})

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}},~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}:\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}res}}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~\mathfrak{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}u}}.

where in the last two equations, the left-hand side is a restriction relative to
\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}
, and on the right-hand side it is relative to
\widetilde{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
.

Theorem 4.41
.

Display respects
\omega
-limits in the simplicial model.

Proof.

This holds essentially by construction of
\omega
-limits therein, plus passing across the translation between different forms of display from
theorem

4.40
.
∎

4.5

S
emantics of semi-simplicial types

Finally, we construct semantics for the displayed coinductive types of
section

3.3
, in particular including
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
.
As with most kinds of coinductive definitions, they are terminal coalgebras of some sort, but in this case they are terminal coalgebras for a
copointed
endofunctor.
We will construct such a terminal coalgebra by a sequential limit construction, assuming that the base (discrete) model admits such limits.

4.5.1
Terminal coalgebras for copointed endofunctors

Definition 4.42
.

A
copointed endofunctor
of a category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
is a functor
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}\to\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
together with a natural transformation
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}}
.
A
coalgebra
for a copointed endofunctor is an object
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
with a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
such that the composite
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
is the identity.
A
terminal coalgebra
is a terminal object of the category of coalgebras.

Note that a coalgebra for a
copointed
endofunctor is not just a coalgebra for its underlying ordinary endofunctor, but satisfies the equation
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
.

As usual, we can obtain terminal coalgebras by a sequential limit construction, when such limits exist.
However, in the copointed case it does not suffice to simply consider the limit of the tower
\cdots\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
; we have to incorporate the transformation
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}
in some way.
The classical way to do this (e.g. the dual of
[
Kel80
]
) is to take
equalisers
at each step.
However, equalisers are difficult to understand homotopy-theoretically, so we replace them by a pullback.
The following definition is a partial dual of
[
Shu19
, Definition 8.6]
.

Definition 4.43
.

Given a natural transformation
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}G}
and a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
in the domain of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}G}
, we write
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widehat{\hom}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f})
for the gap map in the following pullback, assuming that the pullback exists.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\times_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}G}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}G}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}G}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}G}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widehat{\hom}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}G}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}

If the domain and codomain of
F
and
G
have a notion of
‘fibration’
, we say that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}
is a
Quillen pre-fibration
if whenever
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}
is a fibration, so is
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widehat{\hom}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f})
.

For example, we have:

Lemma 4.44
.

In a category of telescopes, consider the fibrations to be the morphisms isomorphic to a dependent projection of some telescope.
Then the transformation
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}evens}}:(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\to(\mathord{\hskip 1.0pt\text{--}\hskip 1.0pt})[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}}~]
from
definition

4.34
is a Quillen pre-fibration.

Proof.

Given a dependent projection
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}
in
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})
, the gap map is isomorphic to the dependent projection of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
:

({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq 1}~]\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}})\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}[~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faKey}}^{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\leq 1}~]).\qed

Theorem 4.45
.

Suppose
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
is a category with a terminal object and a notion of fibration that is stable under pullback, and that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
is a copointed endofunctor of
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}}
is a Quillen pre-fibration.
Suppose also that
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
has limits of inverse
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}
-sequences of fibrations, and that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
preserves these limits.
Then there is a terminal
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra.

Proof.

We define inductively a sequence of objects
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
with morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, of which the terminal
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra will be the limit
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
.
We can think of each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
as an approximation to the terminal coalgebra, with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
extending
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
with additional data making it a better approximation; thus each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
should be a fibration.
Since
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
will be constructed inductively from
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, we can expect it to contain all the data that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}

should
contain that relates to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, and thus we can expect to have a map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
(but not yet to
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
).
To achieve the copointedness condition in the limit for these data, we should demand
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
.
And to ensure that the successive approximations are consistent with each other, we should ask that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
.

In sum, therefore, we will inductively construct a sequence of objects
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, with fibrations
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
and morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
, such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
.

To start with, let
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
, the terminal object, and let
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
, with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
the identity.
Now, assume the data constructed up to level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}>{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
.
The idea is to define
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
to be the
universal
object equipped with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
satisfying the desired equations.
This means it is a limit of some diagram.
The usual way to write that diagram is as the equalizer of the two maps

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-1},}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}

but this does not make it evident that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
is a fibration.
Instead, we can express this same limit as the following pullback:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\times_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widehat{\hom}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n})}

(4.46)

The commutativity of this square says that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
.
And by assumption,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widehat{\hom}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n})
is a fibration, hence so is its pullback
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
.

Now let
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
be the limit of the
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}
-sequence of fibrations

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}\cdots\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\cdots\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}.

Since
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
preserves limits of inverse
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}
-sequences,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is the limit of the corresponding sequence

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\infty}\cdots\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\cdots\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}.

The morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
form fence diagrams:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

composed of the parallelograms
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
from our construction, and naturality squares
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
.
The former induces a map of limits
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
, while by naturality the latter induces
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
.
The universal property of limits implies that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is induced by the composite fence, and since
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
this is

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}3}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}

which induces the identity
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
.
Thus,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra.

Now suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
is another
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra.
We construct inductively maps
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
.
We start with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
the unique morphism, and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
the composite
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
.
Then we induce
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
by the universal property of the pullback defining
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\times_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widehat{\hom}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\right)}

This is valid because using the inductive assumptions about
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
, we have

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}

and

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\right)\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n},

and the two triangles relating to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
show that it has the necessary properties.

Now, the equations
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
imply there is an induced map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
, such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is induced by the composites
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
.
But
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
, and the morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
induce the limit map
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
.
Thus,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra morphism.

Finally, suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is any
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra morphism, so we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
.
Then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}
is uniquely determined by the maps
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, and we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
.
But this equation implies by induction that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
for all
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, hence
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
.
∎

4.5.2
Displayed coinductive types

Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
be a dTT natural model with levels, telescopes, décalage, telescope display, type display respecting
\Pi
-types and universes, and
\Pi
-telescopes.
We will apply
theorem

4.45
in
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})
, in which the fibrations are the morphisms isomorphic to the dependent projection from some telescope,

({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}).

In the presence of levels, the objects of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})
are telescopes at
any
level.

Suppose given the input data for a displayed coinductive type, consisting of

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\in\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}){\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}2}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\centerdot{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}){\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}PSub}}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}}\left(({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\centerdot{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\mid\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}),~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\right).

Categorically, this yields the data of a sort of
‘display polynomial’
, where we indicate fibrations with
\twoheadrightarrow
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\centerdot{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\mid\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\centerdot{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}}

The left vertical map is a fibration because it is isomorphic to the dependent projection

({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}})\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}).

Since everything is in the category of telescopes over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}
, we will omit it from the notation for conciseness, so that the above display polynomial becomes

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\centerdot{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\mid\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\centerdot{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\pi}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}}

This display polynomial then defines a copointed endofunctor of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})
as follows:

\frac{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\left.\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}}\right.}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\left.\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}2}}}\middle/_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}}\right.}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\equiv\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{891755}{661988}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{1054256}{661988}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x^{\prime}}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{891755}{661988}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{1054256}{661988}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}}

Here the
\to
denotes a
\Pi
-telescope (
section

2.5.3
), and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}
denotes meta-abstracted telescope display (

2.6.4

Note that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
is meta-abstracted over

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X})
rather than

The actual

The weakening projection

of this endofunctor, which is evidently a fibration.
More than this, we have:

Lemma 4.47
.

The copointing

Lemma 4.49
.

The endofunctor
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
preserves inverse limits of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}
-sequences of fibrations.

Sketch of proof.

This follows from the
\eta
-rules for inverse limits, together with the fact that display also preserves inverse limits.
∎

Therefore, by
theorem

4.45
, there exists a terminal
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra.
Moreover, since we have assumed that inverse limits are representable by single types, this coalgebra is a type and not just a telescope.
This type is our candidate for the displayed coinductive type; we can unpack its definition as follows.
The construction produces a tower of fibrations
g_{n}
, which is to say a sequence of finite telescopes dependent on the previous ones:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\;\!{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\equiv{\left(\right)}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})

We choose the level of the empty telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}
to be
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\sqcup}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}}
; the explicit description given below then implies that all the other telescopes
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
are also at level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
.

The object

in

Each morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}

By definition of

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

The equation

means that

and

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~],~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})\\
\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~]~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\equiv[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}~]

for some term

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~],~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})\\
\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\begin{multlined}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\\
\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\end{multlined}

Now inspecting the actual construction, we start with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial 0}={\left(\right)}
, the empty telescope, and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial 0})={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\left(\right)}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
.
It is easy to see by induction that the functions
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
then all just project to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
.
For the rest, combining
eqs.

4.46
and
4.48
, we find that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
is defined by

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}\\
\begin{multlined}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~]\equiv\\
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}))\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\end{multlined}

and we have tautologically

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}s}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}.

In particular, by induction we find that in fact each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, though by construction a telescope, is actually just a single type for all
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\geq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
.
Therefore, the tower
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n})
is precisely an infinite telescope as defined in
section

4.1.8
, which we denote

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{X}}=({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}).

Our displayed coinductive type is therefore precisely the limit of this infinite telescope as in
section

4.1.9
:

\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}~[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~]~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lim}}\left({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\widetilde{X}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\right).

Example 4.50
.

Recall that for semi-simplicial types
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
, we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\equiv{\left(\right)}
