\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}

\displaystyle\equiv\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}2}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}

\displaystyle\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0})\to\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.94444pt}{\resizebox{710362}{595649}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.94444pt}{\resizebox{710362}{595649}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.3611pt}{\resizebox{564320}{418919}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.97221pt}{\resizebox{478477}{300445}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.94444pt}{\resizebox{710362}{595649}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.94444pt}{\resizebox{710362}{595649}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.3611pt}{\resizebox{564320}{418919}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.97221pt}{\resizebox{478477}{300445}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;:\;\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}

\displaystyle\equiv\begin{multlined}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0})\to\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.75pt}{\resizebox{825543}{612836}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.25pt}{\resizebox{923794}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathopen{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{(}}}$}}$}}}}}~\rule[-2.5pt]{0.0pt}{10.00002pt}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y})\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\prime\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y})~\mathchoice{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\displaystyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-2.5pt}{\resizebox{898029}{753010}{\hbox{\raisebox{2.5pt}{$\textstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-2.2361pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.75pt}{\resizebox{825543}{612836}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.76805pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.25pt}{\resizebox{923794}{580068}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathclose{\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}\kern-1.49303pt\hbox{${{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{)}}}$}}$}}}}}\\
{}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;:\;\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\prime}}\;:\;\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}{{}^{\prime\prime}}\;:\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\to\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}\;\to\;\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}\end{multlined}

\displaystyle\equiv\begin{multlined}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}001}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}010}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}011}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}001}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}010}$}})\\
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}100}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}0})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}101}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}001}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}100}$}})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}110}$}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}1}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}010}$}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\scalebox{0.55}[1.0]{$\scriptscriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}100}$}})\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}\end{multlined}

This suggests that in general,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
will be the type of
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})
-truncated semi-simplicial types, while
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
will be the type of ways to extend such an
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}
to an
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
-truncated one, i.e. the types of indexed families of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
-simplices.
We will prove this formally in
section

4.5.5
.

It remains to show that this construction of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}dCoind}}
has the structure stipulated in
section

3.3
.
To this end, we first unpack what it means for a type
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Ty}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})
to be an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra.
This means it is equipped with a section of the projection
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C})=({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}))\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}
, which syntactically is to say a partial substitution

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}),{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x^{\prime}}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}).

But this is equivalent to giving its components, which we abstract over
x
to emphasise their dependence on it:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}))\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}

This is evidently precisely the structure of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}head}}
and
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}tail}}
from
section

3.3
.
Thus, our terminal
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra admits these destructors.

Furthermore, to give some other telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})
an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra structure is equivalent to equipping
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta})
with the premises of the corecursor, where the indices-assigning map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}:({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Theta})\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
is the dependent projection.
Thus, terminality of our terminal
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra implies that it admits the corecursor for telescopes
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
of this form.

In the models arising from type-theoretic model toposes, the underlying category is actually locally cartesian closed, and thus the functor
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
can be extended from
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})
to the larger slice category
(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}))/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
, with the same terminal coalgebra in this larger category.
This directly implies the full corecursion principle, since
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}
in that rule equips
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
with the structure of an object of this slice.

In fact, the same is true for arbitrary models: the premises of the corecursor equip
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
with
‘enough of an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra structure’
to deduce the existence of a unique compatible map to the terminal coalgebra.
In the next section we prove this in a more general abstract context.

4.5.3
Terminal generalised coalgebras

Let
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
be a copointed endofunctor of a category
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
as in
section

4.5.1
, where
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
is a full subcategory of some larger category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}E}
.

Definition 4.51
.

An object
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}E}
is a
generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra
if it is equipped with:

•

For any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\in\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
and morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
, a specified morphism
\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
, such that

•

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\circ\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}
.

•

For any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}
in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
, we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}
.

In more abstract language, we can say that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
induces a copointed endofunctor
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}*}
of the functor category
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Set}}^{\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}}
by precomposition, and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
is a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra if the functor
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}E}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y},-):\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Set}}
is an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}^{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}*}
-coalgebra.
The following observation is then a consequence of the Yoneda lemma, but we write it out explicitly.

Lemma 4.52
.

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\in\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
, then generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra structures on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
are bijective to ordinary
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra structures.

Proof.

In one direction, if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
is an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra structure, then given
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
define
\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
.
Then we have

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\circ\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}

and

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}.

In the other direction, given a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra structure, let
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
.
Then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
by assumption, so
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
is an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra structure.
Moreover, the other axiom implies that for any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}
we have
\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
.
Thus one round-trip composite is the identity.
The other round-trip composite simply sends
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}
to
\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y})\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
.
∎

Of course, a
morphism of generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebras
is a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}
such that for any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathsf{Z}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\in\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
we have
\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}
.

Lemma 4.53
.

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}E}
is a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
is an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
, then a morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
is a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra morphism if and only if
\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}
.

Proof.

If it is a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra map, then taking
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
in
\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}
we get
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}
.
On the other hand, if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}
then for any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X^{\prime}}
in
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
we have
\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x^{\prime}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}}
, as desired.
∎

Theorem 4.54
.

Let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
be as in
theorem

4.45
, and let
\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
be a full subcategory of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}E}
such that the embedding preserves the terminal object and the inverse limits of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\omega}
-sequences of fibrations.
Then the terminal
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra constructed in
theorem

4.45
is also a terminal generalised
F
-coalgebra.

Proof.

Indeed, the proof of terminality in
theorem

4.45
really only uses the generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra structure, which we can see clearly by repeating it in that language.
Let
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}E}
be a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra.
We construct inductively maps
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}n}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
.
We start with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
the unique morphism (since
1\in\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}}
is also terminal in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}E}
), and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}
.
Then we induce
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
by the universal property of the pullback defining
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\times_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widehat{\hom}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n})}

This is valid because using the inductive assumptions about
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
and the properties of generalised coalgebras, we have

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\epsilon}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}

and

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}\circ\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}

\displaystyle=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}

\displaystyle=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}-{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}}

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n},

and the two triangles relating to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
show that it has the necessary properties.

Now, the equations
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
imply there is an induced map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
, such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is induced by the composites
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}
.
But
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
, and the morphisms
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
induce the limit map
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
, so
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}}
.
Thus, by
lemma

4.53
,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is an
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra morphism.

Finally, suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
is any
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}
-coalgebra morphism, so we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}}
.
Then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}
is uniquely determined by the maps
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}Y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, and we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}}=\overline{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
.
But this equation implies by induction that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
for all
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
, hence
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\infty}
.
∎

4.5.4
The general corecursor

Suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}})
has the structure of the premises of the corecursor from
section

3.3
:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

Then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}
makes it an object of the slice category
(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}))/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
.
We will apply
theorem

4.54
to the full subcategory
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})\subseteq(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}))/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
.
To that end, we give
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
the structure of a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra as follows.

Suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}\in\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi})
, and suppose we have a map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
in
(\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Tel}}\sslash({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma}\centerdot\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}))/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}
, which is to say

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}).

We want to lift
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}
to
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}F}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}
, which is to say we want to give

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon})

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Gamma},~\text{\faIconFromMacro{faLock}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\triangle\!\square}}\mid({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}),({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:\mathcal{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}B}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\phi}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}))

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{,}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\sigma}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}))~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon})

But such an
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}
is exactly part of the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
, while we can define

{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}t}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\tau}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\upsilon}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}b}).

The final equation in the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
is precisely what is necessary to make this well-typed.
The functoriality condition is immediate from the functoriality of
d
.

Thus
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}
is a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra, and hence it admits a unique generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra morphism to the terminal
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}
.
This is a map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Upsilon}\to({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Phi}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}X})
over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\zeta}
, which is precisely the right type of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}corec}}
.
And by
lemma

4.53
, the fact that it is a generalised
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\widetilde{F}}
-coalgebra map precisely gives it the correct computation rules.

\triangleleft

4.5.5
Correctness of semi-simplicial types

Finally, we will justify our universal characterization of
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
semantically.
Specifically, we will show that when
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}SST}}
is constructed as a displayed coinductive type as in
section

4.5.2
, in a model with
\omega
-limits, it does in fact yield a ‘classifier’ of Reedy fibrant semi-simplicial types in the classical sense.

We begin by constructing such a classifier category-theoretically, and then show that this construction coincides with the one obtained from
section

4.5.2
.
We will assume some familiarity with the classical notions of Reedy fibrant diagrams as in
[
KL21
]
.
For all of this section, we fix a particular universe level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
.

4.5.5.1
Ordered direct categories.

Our category-theoretic construction of diagram classifiers works for presheaves over any ‘direct category’ (i.e. diagrams on any ‘inverse category’).

Definition 4.55
.

A
direct category
is a category such that the relation ‘there is a nonidentity arrow from
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
’ on its objects is well-founded.
A
sieve
in a (direct) category is a full subcategory
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}
such that if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}
, then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}
.
An
ordered direct category
is a
finite
direct category together with (1) a total ordering on its objects such that if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
, and (2) such that for all objects
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
, the set of arrows with codomain
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
has a linear order such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}
for any composable
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}
(hence in particular
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
is the greatest element).

An
ordered presheaf
on a direct category is a finite presheaf together with a linear order on the finite set
\sum_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f})({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})<{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}
whenever the left-hand side makes sense.

An ordered direct category is equivalently the opposite of a (finite) ‘ordered inverse category’ in the sense of
[
KL21
, Definition 3.17]
, together with a suitable total ordering on its objects (we require this so that the order of variables in the classifying context is specified).
Similarly, an ordered presheaf is a ‘finite extension‘
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\emptyset}\hookrightarrow{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
in the sense of
[
KL21
, Definition 3.10]
.

Example 4.56
.

Let
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
be the subcategory of the category
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta^{+}}
from
section

4.2.1
containing the objects
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}}
with
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}
.
Thus
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}l}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\boldsymbol{\rangle}})
is the set of length
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}l}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
binary sequences containing exactly
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}k}+{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{1}}
s.
For fixed
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}l}
we give these morphisms Campion’s ordering, namely the usual ordering of binary numbers.
Then
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Delta_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}n}}
is an ordered direct category.

For
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
we write
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
for the sub-presheaf of the representable
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
consisting of nonidentity morphisms, i.e.
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y})=\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}\neq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\}=\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}\prec{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\}
.

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
is a finite direct category and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
is a finite presheaf on it, there is a new finite direct category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
, called the
collage
of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
, which contains
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
as a full subcategory, together with one new object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star})={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
for all
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
.
Note that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}}
restricted to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
coincides with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
.
Moreover,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
are ordered if and only if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
is.
Moreover, if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
is an ordered direct category of finite height with
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
its object of greatest rank, then
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\cong({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\})\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
.
Thus, we can treat this as an induction principle for ordered direct categories.

4.5.5.2
Classifying contexts.

As our first use of this sort of induction, we construct for each ordered direct category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
a ‘classifying context’ for Reedy fibrant
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
-presheaves.
Specifically, we construct by simultaneous induction:

1.

For each ordered direct category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, a context
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
.
This will be the classifying context of Reedy fibrant
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
-types at level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
.

2.

For each ordered presheaf
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, a telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\;\mathsf{tel}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
.

3.

For each map of ordered presheaves
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}{{}^{\prime}}
(not necessarily order-preserving) on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, a partial substitution
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}{{}^{\prime}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
, varying functorially.

4.

For each object
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, a type
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\;\mathsf{type}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
.

5.

For each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
, inducing by the Yoneda lemma a map
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\beta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\subseteq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
, a term
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}b}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\beta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}~]
, such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}b}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}~]={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}b}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})}
for any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}{{}^{\prime}}
.

6.

For each sieve
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}\subseteq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, a telescope
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}\;\mathsf{tel}_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}lsuc}}\;{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}}
and an isomorphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\cong\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}\right)
.
Morevoer, for all the structure in
2
–
5
, the action of the weakening substitution
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\cong\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}\right)\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}
corresponds to left Kan extension along the inclusion
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}\hookrightarrow{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
.

For
1
, we inductively use
2
and set

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\emptyset}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\left(\right)}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\right).

For
2
, we argue inductively on the linear ordering of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
.
If
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
is empty, we set

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\emptyset}}\equiv{\left(\right)}.

Otherwise,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}=({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\})\cup\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}
where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
is the last element in the ordering; the condition on the ordering ensures that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}
is still an (ordered) presheaf.
By the Yoneda lemma,
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}
induces a map
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\beta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\subseteq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}
, hence by
3
a substitution
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\beta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}
.
Thus, inductively using
4
as well, we can define

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}=\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\beta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}~]\right).

We similarly construct
3
by induction on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
(the domain of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}
).
The case when
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
is empty is trivial.
Otherwise, we inductively have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}{{}^{\prime}}}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}}
, and to extend the codomain to
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
it suffices to give a term in context
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}{{}^{\prime}}}
of type

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\beta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}~][~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}}~]

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\beta}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}}\circ{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\}}~]

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\beta}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})}}~].

For this we can pick
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}b}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})}
, using
5
inductively.
Functoriality follows from the inductive assumption of functoriality in
5
.

For
4
, note that the slice category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
is a sieve in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
containing
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
.
Then it suffices to define
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
in the case of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
, since it can then be weakened to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
using
6
.
In this case we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}=({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\})\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
, so the last variable in
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}
is
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
.
Thus, we can define
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{x}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
to be
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\setminus\{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{x}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
.

For
5
, it suffices to deal with the case when
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}
is the last element in the ordering of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
, since otherwise we can weaken from the sub-presheaf of all elements
\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}
to all of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
, using
3
for the inclusion of this sub-presheaf.
But in this case, the last variable in
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
is
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}~]
, so we can take
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}b}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}a}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}
.
Functoriality follows immediately, as does stability under weakening from initial segments for all the data.

Finally, for
6
we induct on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
.
For a sieve in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
there are two possibilities: it could be
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}
or
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
for some sieve
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}
in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, depending on whether it contains the new object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}
.
(Of course, if it contains
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}
, it must also contain all objects
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y})\neq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\emptyset}
, which is to say that
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
must be left Kan extended from
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}
.)
In these two cases, we define

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}

\displaystyle\equiv\left({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}\right)

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}\quad\text{ weakened to }{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}J}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}.

This completes the construction of the classifying context.
Note in particular that a consequence of
3
is that re-ordering the elements of a presheaf
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
modifies
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
only up to isomorphism.

4.5.5.3
The classifying context is classifying.

To show this, we first construct a ‘universal’ diagram over
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
.
Specifically, in any category with families, we construct simultaneously:

1.

For each ordered direct category
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, a Reedy type
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}
of shape
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
and level
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
over
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
in the sense of
[
KL21
, Definition 3.22]
.

2.

For each ordered presheaf
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, the object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
is the canonical
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
-weighted limit of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}
constructed by the ‘master lemma‘ of
[
KL21
, Lemma 3.11]
.
(In particular, therefore,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}
is the matching object of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}
at
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
.)

3.

The maps
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}
are the functorial action of these limits.

4.

The type
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\mid{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}_{x}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
is the object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
with its fibration to the matching object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{x}}
.

5.

The elements
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}b}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
are the projections from the weighted limit
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
.

The interesting case is
1
, where we weaken the Reedy
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
-type
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}
over
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
to
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}
and then must extend it to a Reedy
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H})
-type by giving a type over the matching object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}}}
.
But
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}}={\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
(weakened to
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
), and so we can use
\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}El}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}A}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
is the newly added variable in
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}
.
The other parts follow essentially tautologically.

Lastly, suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}
is a Reedy
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
-type over any context
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
, and suppose that it is ‘
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
-small’ in the sense that each type
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
over the matching object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}
is classified by a specified map into the universe
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
.
We show by induction on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
that it is classified by a unique map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}~]\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}
.
This is trivial when
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
is empty.
Assuming it to be true for
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}
is a Reedy
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H})
-type over
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
, and its restriction to an
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
-type is classified by a map
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, then to extend this to a map into
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}
we must give a term in context
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\Delta}
of type
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}~]\to\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}Type}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\ell}
.
But matching objects are preserved by substitution, so
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}[~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}c}~]
is the matching object
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}M}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\star}}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}
, and thus this is exactly the data extending
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}C}
to a Reedy
({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\oplus{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H})
-type.

4.5.5.4
Display and décalage of classifying contexts.

Since the data
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
, and so on are concrete finite syntactic objects (for any fixed
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
and so on), the rules in
sections

2.4.4
,
2.4.5
,
2.6.2
and
2.6.5
suffice to completely compute display and décalage on them.
We can characterize the results as follows.

Let
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}
denote the interval category
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0}\xrightarrow{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\xi}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1})
, with two objects and one nonidentity morphism
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\xi}
between them.
Then if
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
is a direct category, so is
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
with the product well-ordering where
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\prec{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}
yields
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})\prec({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})\prec({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y})\prec({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y})
.
If
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
is ordered, we make
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
ordered as follows.
The morphisms in
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
with codomain
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
are bijective to those in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
with codomain
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
, so we inherit that ordering.
And the morphisms in
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
with codomain
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
are two copies of those in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
with codomain
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}
, one copy indexed by
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
and one by
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\xi}
, so we give them the product well-ordering where
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\xi}\prec{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}
: thus from
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g}\prec{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f}
we have
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\xi},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g})\prec({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}g})\prec({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\xi},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f})\prec({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}f})
.

There is an evident projection
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}p}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, inducing by precomposition from any presheaf
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
a presheaf
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}p}^{*}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
on
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
.
Each element of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
, say
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
, then induces two elements
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}p}^{*}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
in
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}(({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}))
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}(({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}))
; we denote these
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})
and
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h})
respectively for clarity.
If
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
is ordered, we induce an ordering on
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}p}^{*}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
by ordering each element of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}(({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}))
before the corresponding element of
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}(({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}))
(which is necessary, since
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\xi}
maps the latter to the former).

We also have an inclusion
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}i_{0}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
defined by
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}i_{0}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})=({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
, which is a sieve.
Left Kan extending along this inclusion takes a presheaf
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
to a presheaf
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}i_{0}})_{!}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
on
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
that is supported only on the objects of the form
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
and has exactly the same elements, hence inherits an ordering as well.

Now we prove by simultaneous induction:

1.

For any
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, we have
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}
.

2.

For any presheaf
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}
on
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, we have
({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}D}}}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}p}^{*}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}i_{0}})_{!}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}
.

3.

This identification is functorial in maps
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\alpha}:{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}\to{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}{{}^{\prime}}
.

4.

For each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}
, we have:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

\displaystyle\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}0},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}

\displaystyle\equiv{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}{{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}ev}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})}

\displaystyle={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}p}^{*}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}\cup\{({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\xi},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1}_{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})\}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\partial\!{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\text{\char 136\relax}}}_{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}

\displaystyle\vdash_{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}sm}}}

\displaystyle\;{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}1},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}

\displaystyle\equiv({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}B}^{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x}){{}^{\mathsf{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}d}}}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}

5.

For each
{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}h}\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}x})
, we have:

\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\gamma}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Gamma}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\mathbb{2}}\times{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}I}},~{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}y}{{}^{\prime}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}\Theta}^{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0}p}^{*}{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}H}}
